genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-01.question: In Genesis 1:2, the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Observe that the Spirit of God is already present before order.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: before the light, the Spirit of God was already hovering over the waters.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 1:2: the Spirit of God was hovering over the waters.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-02.question: In Genesis 1:1, tap who created the heavens and the earth.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-02.learningObjective: Identify God as the author of creation.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-02.feedbackCorrect: God is the subject of the Bible's first sentence: he is the one who creates.

feedbackWrong.a: "No princípio" says when, not who.
feedbackWrong.c: The earth is what was created, not who created.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-02.hint: Look for who does the creating.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-03.question: According to Genesis 1:2, what was the earth like at the beginning?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-03.learningObjective: Observe the initial state of the earth.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-03.feedbackCorrect: The text describes the earth still formless and empty, waiting for God to act.

feedbackWrong.a: Human beings are only created in Genesis 1:27.
feedbackWrong.b: There was darkness; light only comes in Genesis 1:3.
feedbackWrong.c: Plants and animals only appear on the following days (Gen 1:11–25).

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-03.hint: Read the first part of the verse.

options.a: Already inhabited by human beings
options.b: Lit by the sun
options.c: Full of plants and animals
options.d: Formless and empty

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-04.question: Put Genesis 1:2 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's sequence: empty earth, darkness, and the Spirit hovering.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the formless earth; the Spirit appears at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-04.hint: The verse begins with the earth.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-05.question: In Genesis 1:2, what was over the face of the deep?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-05.learningObjective: Remember the opening scene of creation.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-05.feedbackCorrect: Before the light there was darkness over the deep: the starting point God will transform.

feedbackWrong.a: The waters appear at the end of the verse; over the deep there was darkness.
feedbackWrong.b: Light only comes in Genesis 1:3, when God speaks.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-05.hint: What was there before God made the light?

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-06.question: What does Genesis 1:1 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-06.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 1:1 to the idea that God comes before everything.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-06.feedbackCorrect: "No princípio, Deus": he is already there when everything begins.

feedbackWrong.a: The earth has a beginning; only God is before it.
feedbackWrong.c: The text gives the beginning an author: God created.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-01-criador-06.hint: See who is already present in the beginning.

options.a: The earth has always existed
options.b: God exists before everything
options.c: The world begins by chance

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-01.question: In Genesis 1:1–2, the earth appears finished and ordered right after the heavens and the earth are created.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-01.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" marks the contrast: once created, the earth was still formless and empty.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the start of Genesis 1:2: the earth, however, was formless and empty.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-01.hint: Notice the word that links the two verses.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-02.question: In Genesis 1:2, tap the word that marks the contrast with the previous verse.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-02.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast marker in the text.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-02.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" turns the page: God created everything, but the earth was still empty.

feedbackWrong.a: "Havia" only describes what existed; the contrast comes earlier.
feedbackWrong.c: "Sobre" shows place, not contrast.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-02.hint: Look for a short word between commas.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-03.question: How does Genesis 1:2 relate to Genesis 1:1?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-03.learningObjective: Relate the statement of 1:1 to the description in 1:2.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-03.feedbackCorrect: After saying God created everything, the text shows the earth still formless, waiting for him.

feedbackWrong.b: The earth is part of what God created in 1:1.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not tell of two creations; it continues the same scene.
feedbackWrong.d: The text is not about material; it is about what the earth was like.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-03.hint: Think about what "porém" does between the two verses.

options.a: It shows the earth still formless, waiting for God
options.b: It shows the earth appearing without God's action
options.c: It tells of a second creation, made after the first
options.d: It explains what material God used for the heavens

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-04.question: How does the scene move forward in Genesis 1:2–3?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from emptiness to light.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-04.feedbackCorrect: First the emptiness, then God's presence, and then the word that brings light.

feedbackWrong.default: God's word comes last: before it, the emptiness and the Spirit present.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-04.hint: Light is the point of arrival.

options.a: The earth is still empty and dark
options.b: The Spirit of God is over the waters
options.c: God speaks and light comes to be

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-05.question: In Genesis 1:3, what happens right after God speaks?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-05.learningObjective: Understand that God's word brings about what it says.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-05.feedbackCorrect: "E houve luz": God's word is fulfilled at once, without effort or delay.

feedbackWrong.a: It is God who speaks, and what he says happens; there is no request.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says the opposite: light comes to be.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-05.hint: The phrase shows the result of God's word.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-06.question: What links Genesis 1:3 to Psalm 33:9?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-06.learningObjective: Relate creation by the word in Genesis and in the Psalms.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God only has to speak for it to happen.

feedbackWrong.a: What brings things into being is God's word, not chaos.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text speaks of effort: he spoke, and it was done.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-01-criador-06.hint: Compare the verb that opens both passages.

options.a: The world is born from chaos
options.b: God creates by his word
options.c: God creates with effort

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-01.question: Genesis 1:1–2 presents the emptiness and the darkness as the starting point of God's work, not as his rivals.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-01.learningObjective: Interpret the initial emptiness as material for God's work, not a rival.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-01.feedbackCorrect: There is no battle: God creates, and his Spirit hovers over the emptiness to give it form.

feedbackWrong.false: The text shows no struggle; it shows God present over the emptiness, about to act.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-01.hint: See what the Spirit of God is doing.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-02.question: In Genesis 1:2, tap the phrase that shows God present before there was light.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that God is present from the beginning.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-02.feedbackCorrect: The Spirit of God is already there, over the waters, before the first word.

feedbackWrong.a: The darkness describes the earth before light; God's presence comes at the end of the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: The deep describes the setting, not God's presence.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-02.hint: Look for someone, not a place.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-03.question: What reading does Genesis 1:1–2 support about the beginning of the world?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about the world's origin.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-03.feedbackCorrect: The text opens with God creating, and his Spirit already hovers over the empty earth.

feedbackWrong.b: The Spirit present over the waters rules out a distant God.
feedbackWrong.c: Nothing appears before God: "No princípio, Deus criou".
feedbackWrong.d: There is no battle: the Spirit hovers in peace over the waters.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-03.hint: Compare each option with the start and end of the passage.

options.a: God is before everything and present from the start
options.b: God made the world and then withdrew from it
options.c: Chaos existed before God, as matter with no owner
options.d: The emptiness is a rival force God must defeat

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-04.question: What sequence reveals the path of light that begins in Genesis 1:3?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-04.learningObjective: See Genesis 1:3 as the start of a thread running through the Bible.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-04.feedbackCorrect: The light of creation points to God's light in the heart and, at last, to eternal light.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1:3), faith (2 Cor 4:6) and eternity (Rev 22:5).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible's story: creation, church, eternity.

options.a: God says "Let there be light", and light exists
options.b: God makes his light shine in the hearts of believers
options.c: In the eternal city, God himself is the light

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-05.question: In Genesis 1:1, which verb shows what God does in the beginning?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-05.feedbackCorrect: In the text, only God is the subject of this verb: he brings into being, not just arranges.

feedbackWrong.a: Organizing assumes something already there; the text says God made the heavens and earth.
feedbackWrong.c: God does not find the world ready; he brings it into being.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-05.hint: It is the verb that names the scene.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-06.question: What links Genesis 1:1 to John 1:3?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-06.learningObjective: Connect creation in Genesis to the person of Christ, as the NT does.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-06.feedbackCorrect: John rereads Genesis: the Word, Jesus, was in the beginning and all was made through him.

feedbackWrong.a: John speaks of the same creation as Genesis, not another one.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text mentions angels; all things were made through the Word.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-01-criador-06.hint: See what John says about through whom all things were made.

options.a: A second creation of the world
options.b: Christ present at creation
options.c: Angels helping God create

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-01.question: In Genesis 1:8, God gives the expanse the name Earth.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-01.learningObjective: Observe the name God gives the expanse on the second day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-01.feedbackCorrect: The expanse is named Heavens; the dry land is only called Earth in 1:10.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the start of 1:8: God called the expanse Heavens. Earth is the dry land's name (1:10).

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-01.hint: See the name that comes right after "expansão".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-02.question: In Genesis 1:16, tap the light that rules the night.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-02.learningObjective: Identify the role of each light in Genesis 1:16.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-02.feedbackCorrect: The lesser light rules the night; the greater, the day. God gives each its role.

feedbackWrong.a: In 1:16 the stars come at the end, with no role of their own; another rules the night.
feedbackWrong.b: The greater one rules the day, not the night.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-02.hint: Read the part of the verse that speaks of the night.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-03.question: According to Genesis 1:22, what does God do with the sea creatures and the birds?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-03.learningObjective: Observe that God blesses the living creatures of the fifth day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-03.feedbackCorrect: God blesses them and tells them to multiply: new life comes with blessing.

feedbackWrong.a: Naming the animals comes later, with Adam (Gen 2:19).
feedbackWrong.b: Gathering in one place is a command to the waters (1:9); here God says to fill the seas.
feedbackWrong.c: Human dominion only appears in 1:26–28, on the sixth day.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-03.hint: Read the start of the verse.

options.a: Gives each of them a name
options.b: Tells them to stay in one place
options.c: Places them under human dominion
options.d: Blesses them and tells them to multiply

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-04.question: Put Genesis 1:9 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-04.feedbackCorrect: First the command to the waters, then the dry land, and finally the fulfillment.

feedbackWrong.default: The command comes before the fulfillment: "E assim se fez" closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-04.hint: The verse ends by showing the result.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-05.question: In Genesis 1:24, which animals does the land produce along with creeping things and wild animals?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-05.learningObjective: Remember the creatures the land produces on the sixth day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-05.feedbackCorrect: On day six the land produces livestock, creeping things and wild animals: dry-land creatures.

feedbackWrong.a: Birds belong to the fifth day as well (1:20–21).
feedbackWrong.c: Fish come from the waters, on the fifth day (1:20–21).

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-05.hint: Think of the animals that live on dry land.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-06.question: What does Genesis 1:25 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-06.learningObjective: Connect the refrain "era bom" to God's approval.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-06.feedbackCorrect: "Deus viu que isso era bom": God's verdict on his work is approval.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no correction: the text says it was good.
feedbackWrong.c: God looks at his work; he does not abandon it.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-02-dias-06.hint: See what God does at the end of the verse.

options.a: God approves what he made
options.b: God fixes what went wrong
options.c: God sets his work aside

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-01.question: In Genesis 1:11–12, the land produces plants because God commanded it, not on its own initiative.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-01.learningObjective: Understand that the land's fruitfulness responds to God's word.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-01.feedbackCorrect: The command comes first (1:11) and the land responds (1:12): it produces what God ordered.

feedbackWrong.false: See the sequence: God says "Que a terra produza", and only then did the land produce.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-01.hint: Compare the start of 1:11 with the start of 1:12.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-02.question: In Genesis 1:14, tap the word that links the lights to their purpose.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-02.learningObjective: Recognize the purpose relationship in Genesis 1:14.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-02.feedbackCorrect: "Para" introduces the purpose: the lights exist to serve, separating and marking time.

feedbackWrong.a: "Haja" is the command that brings the lights; their purpose comes after.
feedbackWrong.c: "Expansão" says where the lights are, not what they are for.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-02.hint: Look for the word repeated before each purpose.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-03.question: In Genesis 1:20–21, how does what God says relate to what God does?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-03.learningObjective: Relate God's word to his creative action.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-03.feedbackCorrect: In 1:20 God tells the waters to teem; in 1:21 he himself creates sea creatures and birds.

feedbackWrong.a: In 1:21 the subject is God: "E Deus criou".
feedbackWrong.b: The work follows right away, in the next verse.
feedbackWrong.d: What God does matches what he said: sea creatures and birds.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-03.hint: Compare the subject of the verbs in 1:20 and in 1:21.

options.a: The waters produce life alone, without God acting
options.b: God commands, but leaves the work for later
options.c: God himself does what he has just announced
options.d: God announces one thing and does something else

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-04.question: How does the third day unfold in Genesis 1:12–13?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-04.learningObjective: Understand the pattern repeated on each day.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-04.feedbackCorrect: The land responds, God approves and the day closes: a rhythm repeated across the days.

feedbackWrong.default: God's approval comes after the work, and "tarde e manhã" closes the day.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-04.hint: The day only ends after God evaluates the work.

options.a: The land produces what God commanded
options.b: God sees that it is good
options.c: The day ends with evening and morning

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-05.question: In Genesis 1:4, what does God do with the light and the darkness?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-05.learningObjective: Understand separating as an action that orders creation.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-05.feedbackCorrect: Separating is the first act of order: light and darkness get distinct places.

feedbackWrong.a: Nothing is hidden: light and darkness remain, each in its place.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not say light comes out of darkness; God distinguishes them, each in its place.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-05.hint: It is the action that gives each thing its place.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-06.question: What links Genesis 1:5 to Psalm 74:16?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-06.learningObjective: Relate God's naming to his rule over time.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-06.feedbackCorrect: Whoever names the day and the night owns them, and the psalm confirms it: they are God's.

feedbackWrong.b: The psalm says the opposite: "the night is yours".
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text gives the day to the sun; the psalmist says "The day is yours".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-02-dias-06.hint: Compare who gives the names in Genesis with whom the psalm gives the day to.

options.a: Day and night belong to God
options.b: The night belongs to darkness
options.c: The sun owns the day

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-01.question: Genesis 1:17–18 presents the heavenly bodies as powers that rule on their own and deserve reverence.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-01.learningObjective: Distinguish the text's reading from the idea of stars as powers to revere.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-01.feedbackCorrect: God places them in the sky, with tasks: to give light, mark time and separate light and dark.

feedbackWrong.true: The lights are works God placed there to serve; the text gives them no will and no worship.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-01.hint: See who places the lights in the sky and why.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-02.question: In Genesis 1:21, tap the phrase that shows even the greatest sea creatures are God's work.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that nothing in the sea is God's rival.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-02.feedbackCorrect: "Deus criou": not even the sea's giants are outside his work. They are creatures, not rivals.

feedbackWrong.a: That phrase says where they live, not who made them.
feedbackWrong.c: That phrase names the creatures but does not say where they come from.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-02.hint: Look for who acts on these creatures, not their name.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-03.question: What reading does the refrain "Deus viu que isso era bom" support about the created world?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-03.learningObjective: Interpret the refrain "era bom" as God's approval of material creation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-03.feedbackCorrect: God evaluates his work and calls it good, even before human beings exist.

feedbackWrong.a: The land produces because God commands (1:24), and God makes the animals (1:25).
feedbackWrong.c: God's verdict comes before human beings are created (1:26).
feedbackWrong.d: God looks at land, plants and animals and says they are good.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-03.hint: See who evaluates the work and when that happens.

options.a: The land produces life on its own; God only watches
options.b: The created world is good because God made and approves it
options.c: Animals are only good because they serve human beings
options.d: Matter is worth little; only the spiritual has value

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-04.question: What sequence reveals how the days answer Genesis 1:2?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-04.learningObjective: Interpret the days as God's answer to the formless and empty earth.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-04.feedbackCorrect: To what was formless, God gives form (days 1–3); what was empty, he fills (days 4–6).

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the problem in 1:2; God first gives form, then fills what he formed.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-04.hint: Think of the two marks of the earth in 1:2.

options.a: The earth is formless and empty
options.b: God separates and shapes sky, sea and land
options.c: God fills these spaces with lights and living things

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-05.question: In Genesis 1:11, which word shows that plants follow an order given by God?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-05.learningObjective: Remember the term showing the order God gives to living things.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-05.feedbackCorrect: "Segundo a sua espécie": life has form and limits given by God; it is not confusion.

feedbackWrong.a: Seasons only appear with the lights (1:14); here the standard is different.
feedbackWrong.c: Plants do not follow their own will; they follow the order God gave them.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-05.hint: It is the word repeated many times on days 3, 5 and 6.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-06.question: What links Genesis 1:20 to Isaiah 45:18?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-06.learningObjective: Connect the filling of creation to God's purpose of an inhabited earth.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-06.feedbackCorrect: God fills water, sky and land with life; Isaiah explains: he did not make the world to be empty.

feedbackWrong.b: Both texts show the opposite: God does not leave the earth empty.
feedbackWrong.c: In Genesis it is God's word that fills the waters, not chaos.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-02-dias-06.hint: Compare what God wants for the waters with what Isaiah says about the earth.

options.a: An earth made to be inhabited
options.b: God leaves the chaos as it is
options.c: Life arises from chaos

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-01.question: In Genesis 1:27, the verb "criou" appears three times.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-01.learningObjective: Observe the repetition of the verb create in Genesis 1:27.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-01.feedbackCorrect: "Criou" is repeated three times: the text insists humans are God's direct work.

feedbackWrong.false: Count again: "Deus criou o homem", "o criou" and "os criou". That is three times.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-01.hint: Read the verse slowly and count the verb.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-02.question: In Genesis 1:28, tap what God tells the man and the woman to fill.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-02.learningObjective: Identify what God commands to be filled in Genesis 1:28.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-02.feedbackCorrect: God tells them to fill the earth: the blessing includes multiplying and spreading over the world.

feedbackWrong.a: The fish are on the list of what to rule, not what to fill.
feedbackWrong.c: The birds are also part of what to rule; they are not what God says to fill.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-02.hint: See the command that comes after "multipliquem-se".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-03.question: According to Genesis 1:26, over what will human beings have dominion?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-03.learningObjective: Observe the scope of the dominion given to human beings.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-03.feedbackCorrect: The list runs from fish to creeping things and includes all the earth; not other people.

feedbackWrong.a: The list has only creatures; no one is given dominion over another human.
feedbackWrong.b: The sun, moon and stars are not on the list; they rule day and night (1:16).
feedbackWrong.c: Livestock are on the list, but it also includes fish, birds, creeping things and all the earth.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-03.hint: Read the list that comes after "domínio".

options.a: Other human beings, as servants
options.b: The sun, the moon and the stars of the sky
options.c: Only domestic animals
options.d: Fish, birds, animals and all the earth

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-04.question: Put Genesis 1:27 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-04.feedbackCorrect: The verse moves from man created in God's image to "homem e mulher os criou".

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with God creating man and ends by naming male and female.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-04.hint: The verse ends by naming the two.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-05.question: In Genesis 1:26, which animals appear on the list between the birds of the sky and all the earth?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-05.learningObjective: Remember the list of creatures under human dominion.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-05.feedbackCorrect: "Animais domésticos" completes the list: dominion reaches every kind of creature.

feedbackWrong.a: Wild animals appear in 1:24–25; this list names others.
feedbackWrong.c: The sea creatures are already at the start of the list, as "peixes do mar".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-05.hint: Think of the animals that live near people.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-06.question: What does Genesis 1:27 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-06.learningObjective: Connect the image of God to the unique place of humans in creation.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-06.feedbackCorrect: No other creature receives these words: human beings have a unique place.

feedbackWrong.a: Image is not equality: humans reflect God but remain creatures.
feedbackWrong.c: Animals come "segundo as suas espécies"; only humans come in God's image.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-03-imagem-06.hint: Compare human beings with the other works in the chapter.

options.a: A being equal to God
options.b: A unique place in creation
options.c: Just one more animal among others

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-01.question: In Genesis 1:26, God creates human beings with the same command he used for the animals.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the creation of animals and of humans.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-01.feedbackCorrect: Here God does not say "Que a terra produza", as in 1:24, but "Façamos": personal creation.

feedbackWrong.true: For the animals, God says "Que a terra produza" (1:24); here, "Façamos o homem".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-01.hint: Compare how God begins to speak here and in 1:24.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-02.question: In Genesis 1:28, tap the action of God that comes before any task.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-02.learningObjective: Recognize that the blessing comes before the task.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-02.feedbackCorrect: First comes the blessing; only then the task. What God asks flows from what he gives.

feedbackWrong.a: "Dominem" is the last command in the verse, not God's first action.
feedbackWrong.b: "Encham" is already part of the task, said after the blessing.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-02.hint: Look at the start of the verse, before the quotation marks.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-03.question: In Genesis 1:26–27, how does the image of God relate to dominion?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-03.learningObjective: Relate the image of God to the task of ruling creation.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-03.feedbackCorrect: God makes humans in his image and, in the same speech, gives them a task: to rule on his behalf.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of strength; dominion is given by God.
feedbackWrong.b: The order is reversed: first the image, then dominion as a task.
feedbackWrong.d: God is still the one who gives dominion; humans rule under him.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-03.hint: See what comes first in God's speech in 1:26.

options.a: Dominion comes because humans are stronger than animals
options.b: Dominion is what makes humans the image of God
options.c: Dominion is the task of those made in God's image
options.d: God hands over dominion and stops ruling the world

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-04.question: How do the movements of Genesis 1:27–28 link together?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-04.learningObjective: Understand the link between creation, blessing and task.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-04.feedbackCorrect: First God creates, then he blesses and, finally, entrusts the earth to those he made.

feedbackWrong.default: The blessing sits between creation and task: God creates, blesses and then entrusts.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-04.hint: The task is the last movement.

options.a: God creates human beings in his image
options.b: God blesses the man and the woman
options.c: God entrusts them with caring for the earth

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-05.question: In Genesis 1:28, which verb goes with the command to fill the earth?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-05.learningObjective: Understand the task that comes with the blessing.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-05.feedbackCorrect: To subdue is to bring the earth into order under God's rule, like managing what is his.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not tell them to fear the earth; humans are called to govern it.
feedbackWrong.c: God does not tell them to abandon the earth; he says to fill it and care for it.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-05.hint: It is the command that comes right after filling.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-06.question: What links Genesis 1:26 to Psalm 8:6?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-06.learningObjective: Relate dominion in Genesis to the praise of Psalm 8.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts, God gives the dominion; the works still belong to his hands.

feedbackWrong.a: The psalm says "You made him ruler": dominion is given, not seized.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts speak of human beings, not angels.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-03-imagem-06.hint: See who makes humans exercise dominion in the psalm.

options.a: Dominion won by force
options.b: Dominion received from God
options.c: Angels' dominion over the world

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-01.question: In Genesis 1:28, human dominion appears as a task received from God, not a right won.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-01.learningObjective: Interpret dominion as care received from God, not exploitation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-01.feedbackCorrect: Dominion comes within the blessing and by God's word: a gift with responsibility.

feedbackWrong.false: Humans win nothing here: God blesses and tells them what to do.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-01.hint: See who speaks and what happens before the commands.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-02.question: In Genesis 1:27, tap the phrase that shows the image of God does not belong to the man alone.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that male and female are equally God's image.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-02.feedbackCorrect: "Homem e mulher os criou" closes the sentence on the image: both bear it together.

feedbackWrong.b: "O homem" here means humankind; the verse then explains who they are.
feedbackWrong.c: That phrase speaks of the image but does not say who receives it.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-02.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-03.question: What reading does Genesis 1:27 support about the worth of each person?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about human dignity.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-03.feedbackCorrect: Dignity comes from God's act, not human deeds, and it applies to male and female.

feedbackWrong.a: Humans have done nothing yet: the image is given before any task.
feedbackWrong.b: Reflecting God is not being God: the text repeats that humans were created.
feedbackWrong.d: The text says "homem e mulher os criou", right after speaking of the image.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-03.hint: Think of who acts in the verse and who receives the image.

options.a: A person's worth depends on what they produce or achieve
options.b: Being God's image makes humans little gods
options.c: Every person has dignity because they were made in God's image
options.d: Only the man reflects God; the woman comes second

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-04.question: What sequence reveals the path of God's image through the Bible?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-04.learningObjective: See the image of God as a thread running through the Bible.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-04.feedbackCorrect: The image begins at creation, still holds after the flood and is renewed in Christ.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1:27), flood (Gen 9:6) and new life in Christ (Col 3:10).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible's story: creation, flood, church.

options.a: God creates male and female in his image
options.b: After the flood, human life is still protected by that image
options.c: In Christ, God's image is renewed in those who believe

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-05.question: In Genesis 1:26, which word sums up what human beings reflect of God?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the scene's theological meaning.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-05.feedbackCorrect: "Imagem": humans were made to reflect who God is, like a living portrait.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of measure; it speaks of something that reflects God.
feedbackWrong.b: God acts by his will, but the text says something else about how humans are made.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-05.hint: It is the word the next verse repeats twice.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-06.question: What links Genesis 1:26 to James 3:9?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-06.learningObjective: Connect the image of God to respect for every person.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-06.feedbackCorrect: James draws the conclusion: those made in God's likeness must not be cursed.

feedbackWrong.a: James is not talking about appearance but about the worth of those God made.
feedbackWrong.c: James speaks of people in general, not only believers.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-03-imagem-06.hint: See why James thinks cursing someone is serious.

options.a: Likeness is only appearance
options.b: Respect for those who reflect God
options.c: Only believers reflect God

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-01.question: In Genesis 2:2, God rests from only part of the work he had done.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-01.learningObjective: Observe that God rests from all his work.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says "de toda a sua obra": nothing was left half-done when God rested.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of 2:2: God rested "de toda a sua obra que fizera".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-01.hint: See how much of the work is mentioned at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-02.question: In Genesis 2:3, tap what God blessed.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-02.learningObjective: Identify what God blesses in Genesis 2:3.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-02.feedbackCorrect: God blesses a day: time itself receives his blessing.

feedbackWrong.b: That phrase speaks of what God did, not what he blessed.
feedbackWrong.c: The work is what God rested from; what he blesses is something else.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-02.hint: Look for what comes right after "abençoou".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-03.question: According to Genesis 2:1, what was completed?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-03.learningObjective: Observe that the whole creation was completed.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-03.feedbackCorrect: Heavens, earth and "all their host", everything that fills them, reach the end of the work.

feedbackWrong.a: There is no second part: everything was completed.
feedbackWrong.b: Eden only appears in Genesis 2:8; here it is the whole creation.
feedbackWrong.d: The text speaks of the heavens and the earth, and all that fills them.

options.a: The first part of creation
options.b: The garden of Eden and its rivers
options.c: The heavens, the earth and all that fills them
options.d: Only the earth, prepared for human beings

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-04.question: Put Genesis 2:2 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-04.feedbackCorrect: First God finishes the work, then he rests, and the text says from what: from all of it.

feedbackWrong.default: Finishing comes before resting; the end of the verse says what God rested from.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-04.hint: The verse begins with the work finished.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-05.question: In Genesis 2:3, by what title does the text refer to God?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-05.learningObjective: Remember how the text refers to God on the seventh day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-05.feedbackCorrect: "Como Criador": the text reminds us that all the work God rests from is his.

feedbackWrong.a: "Senhor Deus" appears in 2:4; in 2:3 the title is different.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not call God King here; it highlights who did the work.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-05.hint: The title has to do with the work God has just finished.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-06.question: What does Genesis 2:1 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-06.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 2:1 to the idea that God completes what he begins.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-06.feedbackCorrect: "Foram completados": God carries the work to the end, leaving nothing half-done.

feedbackWrong.a: God is the one who finishes the work (2:2), not the world itself.
feedbackWrong.c: The text says the opposite: everything was completed.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-04-descanso-06.hint: See what happened to the heavens and the earth.

options.a: The world completed itself
options.b: God's work is complete
options.c: Creation was left half-done

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-01.question: In Genesis 2:1–2, God's rest comes as the result of a work already complete.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-01.learningObjective: Understand the relationship between completed work and rest.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-01.feedbackCorrect: First everything was completed (2:1); then, having finished, God rested (2:2).

feedbackWrong.false: See the order: "foram completados" and "tendo Deus terminado" come before "descansou".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-01.hint: Compare what happens in 2:1 with what God does in 2:2.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-02.question: In Genesis 2:3, tap the word that explains why God blessed the seventh day.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause relationship in Genesis 2:3.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-02.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" gives the reason: the day is blessed because on it God rested.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nele" points to the day, but another word introduces the reason.
feedbackWrong.b: "Como" introduces God's title, Creator, not the reason for the blessing.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-02.hint: Look right after the comma that follows "santificou".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-03.question: In Genesis 2:2–3, what sets the seventh day apart from the six before it?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-03.learningObjective: Relate the seventh day to the six days of work.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-03.feedbackCorrect: On the six days God speaks and makes; on the seventh he stops, blesses and sanctifies the day.

feedbackWrong.a: Human beings were created on the sixth day (1:27–31).
feedbackWrong.c: There was nothing to fix: everything was very good (1:31).
feedbackWrong.d: That blessing belongs to the fifth day (1:22); here God blesses a day.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-03.hint: Compare what God does on the seventh day with what he did before.

options.a: God creates human beings on that day
options.b: God stops creating and blesses the day
options.c: God fixes what had gone wrong
options.d: God blesses the animals and the birds

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-04.question: How does the seventh day unfold in Genesis 2:2–3?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-04.learningObjective: Understand the movements of the seventh day.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-04.feedbackCorrect: God finishes and rests; then he blesses the day and sets it apart for himself.

feedbackWrong.default: Rest comes first; blessing and setting the day apart come after.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-04.hint: The blessing only comes after the work is done.

options.a: God finishes the work and rests
options.b: God blesses the seventh day
options.c: God sets the day apart for himself

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-05.question: In Genesis 2:2, what state was the work in when God rested?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-05.learningObjective: Understand the sequence between finishing and resting.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-05.feedbackCorrect: "Tendo Deus terminado": rest comes after the work is finished, not in the middle of it.

feedbackWrong.b: Nothing was interrupted; the text says the work was complete (2:1).
feedbackWrong.c: The work was not just starting: it filled the six days before.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-05.hint: See what 2:1 says about the heavens and the earth.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-06.question: What links Genesis 2:3 to Exodus 20:11?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-06.learningObjective: Relate the seventh day of creation to Israel's Sabbath.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-06.feedbackCorrect: Exodus grounds the Sabbath in Genesis: the people work six days and rest, like God.

feedbackWrong.a: Exodus ties the Sabbath to creation: "in six days the Lord made".
feedbackWrong.b: The Sabbath is not a reward: Exodus grounds it in what God did.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-04-descanso-06.hint: See the reason Exodus gives for the Sabbath.

options.a: A rule unrelated to creation
options.b: Rest as a reward for effort
options.c: A rhythm of work and rest

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-01.question: Genesis 2:2 shows that God rested because he was tired after six days of work.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-01.learningObjective: Distinguish God's rest from the idea of tiredness.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-01.feedbackCorrect: The text ties rest to the work's completion, not fatigue; God does not grow tired (Isa 40:28).

feedbackWrong.true: The reason is in the verse itself: "tendo Deus terminado". Nothing there speaks of tiredness.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-01.hint: See what happens to the work before the rest.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-02.question: In Genesis 2:1, tap the word that shows God rested because the work was finished.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that rest comes from finished work.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-02.feedbackCorrect: "Completados": the rest in 2:2 rests on a work that reached its end.

feedbackWrong.a: "Exército" says what fills heaven and earth, not the state of the work.
feedbackWrong.c: "Os céus" says what was made, not whether the work was finished.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-02.hint: Look for the word that says what state the work was in.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-03.question: What reading does Genesis 2:2–3 support about God's rest?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God's rest.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-03.feedbackCorrect: God stops before the finished work and blesses the day: the rest of one who has completed.

feedbackWrong.a: God blesses and sanctifies the day; it is not a farewell to the world.
feedbackWrong.b: The text gives the reason: finished work, not fatigue (Isa 40:28).
feedbackWrong.c: It is the only day God blesses and sanctifies.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-03.hint: Compare each option with what God does after resting.

options.a: God withdrew and left the world to run on its own
options.b: God stopped from tiredness, as we stop at day's end
options.c: The seventh day is worth less, since nothing is created on it
options.d: God stops because the work is complete, and blesses the day

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-04.question: What sequence reveals the path of the rest of Genesis 2:3 through the Bible?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-04.learningObjective: See the rest in Genesis as the start of a thread running through the Bible.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-04.feedbackCorrect: God's rest becomes Israel's Sabbath, and Jesus shows it is a gift, not a burden.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 2:3), law (Exod 20:11) and Jesus' teaching (Mark 2:27).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible's story: creation, law, Gospels.

options.a: God rests on the seventh day and blesses it
options.b: The Sabbath is given to Israel following creation's rhythm
options.c: Jesus teaches that the Sabbath exists for people's good

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-05.question: In Genesis 2:3, which verb shows that God set the seventh day apart for himself?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the scene's theological meaning.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-05.feedbackCorrect: To sanctify is to set apart for God: the seventh day now belongs to him in a special way.

feedbackWrong.a: The day is not closed off; it is blessed and set apart.
feedbackWrong.c: God named day and night in 1:5; here the verb is different.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-05.hint: It is the verb that comes with blessing.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-06.question: What links Genesis 2:2 to Hebrews 4:10?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-06.learningObjective: Connect God's rest to the invitation given to his people.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews shows God's rest did not stay on the seventh day: it is offered to his people.

feedbackWrong.a: Hebrews says a rest still remains for the people of God (4:9).
feedbackWrong.c: Hebrews speaks of resting from one's own works, not earning rest by them.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-04-descanso-06.hint: See who, in Hebrews, enters God's rest.

options.a: A rest that stayed in the past
options.b: An invitation into God's rest
options.c: Rest earned by one's own effort

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-01.question: In Genesis 2:9, the tree of life stood at the entrance of the garden.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-01.learningObjective: Observe where the tree of life stood.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-01.feedbackCorrect: The tree of life was in the middle of the garden, not at the entrance.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Genesis 2:9: the tree of life was in the middle of the garden.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-01.hint: See where the text places the tree of life.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-02.question: In Genesis 2:10, tap what flowed out of Eden to water the garden.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-02.learningObjective: Observe that the garden is watered by a river.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-02.feedbackCorrect: A river flows out of Eden: the garden's water comes from the very place God prepared.

feedbackWrong.a: The four branches come later, when the river divides.
feedbackWrong.c: The garden is what receives the water, not what flows out of Eden.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-02.hint: Look for who does the action of "saía".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-03.question: According to Genesis 2:9, what were the trees God made grow like?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-03.learningObjective: Observe the goodness and beauty of the garden.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-03.feedbackCorrect: Beauty and food: the garden is good for the eyes and for life.

feedbackWrong.a: Only one tree will be forbidden (2:17); the others were good to eat.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord God makes the trees grow, not the man.
feedbackWrong.d: The text says the trees were good for food.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-03.hint: Read the description right after "toda árvore".

options.a: All forbidden to the man
options.b: Pleasing to the eye and good for food
options.c: Planted by the man near the river
options.d: Tall, but with no fruit to eat

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-04.question: Put Genesis 2:9 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-04.feedbackCorrect: First the trees in general, then the two trees in the middle of the garden.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the trees in general; the tree of knowledge comes last.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-04.hint: Go from the general to the specific.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-05.question: In Genesis 2:8, what does the Lord God do in Eden before placing the man there?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-05.learningObjective: Remember that the garden is God's work.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-05.feedbackCorrect: God plants the garden: the man's place is prepared by God, as a gift.

feedbackWrong.a: The garden is not found ready-made: the Lord God himself plants it.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not mention a fence; it speaks of God making a garden.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-05.hint: Think of what a gardener does.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-06.question: What does Genesis 2:15 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-06.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 2:15 to work as a calling that comes before the fall.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-06.feedbackCorrect: God himself puts the man in the garden to work it: work comes from his hands.

feedbackWrong.a: The garden is a gift, but it comes with a task: to work it and keep it.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord God, who places the man in the garden, defines the task.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-05-eden-06.hint: See who puts the man in the garden, and for what purpose.

options.a: The garden makes all work unnecessary
options.b: Work is a task given by God
options.c: The man invents his own trade

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-01.question: In Genesis 2:8, the garden is already planted when God places the man in it.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-01.learningObjective: Understand that God prepares the place before placing the man.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-01.feedbackCorrect: First God plants, then he places the man: the gift comes before the task.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 2:8: the Lord God planted a garden and placed the man there.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-01.hint: See the order of the verse's two verbs.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-02.question: In Genesis 2:15, tap the word that introduces God's purpose in placing the man in the garden.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-02.learningObjective: Recognize the purpose marker in Genesis 2:15.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-02.feedbackCorrect: "Para" opens the purpose: the man is in the garden to work it and keep it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Colocou" says where God put the man; the purpose comes right after.
feedbackWrong.c: "Tomou" is God's first action; the purpose comes at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-02.hint: Look for the word that answers "for what purpose?".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-03.question: In Genesis 2:10–11, what does the river's course show about Eden?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-03.learningObjective: Relate the river of Eden to the lands around it.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-03.feedbackCorrect: The river rises in Eden, waters the garden and branches out: its water reaches other lands.

feedbackWrong.a: The river does not isolate: it branches and flows around other lands, like Havilah.
feedbackWrong.c: It is the opposite: the river flows out of Eden and then divides.
feedbackWrong.d: The text shows the river leaving Eden for other lands, not marking a border.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-03.hint: Follow the river: where it starts and where it goes.

options.a: The river cuts Eden off from the rest of the earth
options.b: The garden's water flows on and reaches other lands
options.c: The garden gets water from the neighboring lands
options.d: The river only marks the garden's border

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-04.question: How does the scene move forward in Genesis 2:8–9?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-04.learningObjective: Understand how the text presents the garden.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-04.feedbackCorrect: First the place and its dweller; then the abundance of trees; finally, the two in the middle.

feedbackWrong.default: Verse 8 brings the garden and the man; the two middle trees close verse 9.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-04.hint: Start with who plants the garden.

options.a: God plants the garden and places the man in it
options.b: Beautiful trees spring up, good for food
options.c: In the middle, the tree of life and that of knowledge

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-05.question: In Genesis 2:10, what is the purpose of the river that flows out of Eden?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-05.learningObjective: Understand the river's purpose in the garden.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-05.feedbackCorrect: The river exists to water the garden: God provides what sustains life there.

feedbackWrong.a: The river divides later, outside the garden; its purpose in the garden is different.
feedbackWrong.c: The river is not a fence; it flows out of Eden to water the garden.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-05.hint: Think of what a garden needs to receive from a river.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-06.question: What links Genesis 2:15 to Colossians 3:23?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-06.learningObjective: Relate the calling in Eden to work done for the Lord.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-06.feedbackCorrect: Since Eden, work is service to God; Paul asks that it be done for the Lord.

feedbackWrong.b: The garden is a gift before the work; and Paul speaks of serving, not earning.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts speak of work and value it as service.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-05-eden-06.hint: Think of who is served by the work in both texts.

options.a: Work done for the Lord
options.b: Work to earn the garden
options.c: Rest with no task at all

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-01.question: In Genesis 2:15, the man receives the garden as its owner, free to use it as he pleases.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-01.learningObjective: Interpret the human calling as care, not ownership.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-01.feedbackCorrect: The garden belongs to the one who planted it (2:8); the man is placed there to work and keep it.

feedbackWrong.true: The text gives a task: to work and keep the garden, not to use it as an owner.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-01.hint: See the purpose God gives the man.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-02.question: In Genesis 2:9, tap the phrase that shows God offers life in the garden.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that life in the garden is God's gift.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-02.feedbackCorrect: In the middle of the garden God places the tree of life: life is a gift that comes from him.

feedbackWrong.a: "Agradável à vista" speaks of beauty; the text points to life elsewhere.
feedbackWrong.c: The tree of knowledge is the tree of the limit (2:17), not the tree of life.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-02.hint: Read the names of the two middle trees carefully.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-03.question: What reading does Genesis 2:15 support about human work?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about work.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-03.feedbackCorrect: Before any sin, God sets the man to work and keep the garden: work is his calling.

feedbackWrong.a: The garden already had food (2:9); work is care, not just survival.
feedbackWrong.c: Disobedience only comes in Genesis 3; here work is already given by God.
feedbackWrong.d: Working the land is a task God himself gave; it is also service to him.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-03.hint: See when and by whom work is given.

options.a: Work is only for survival
options.b: Caring for the garden is God's calling before sin
options.c: Work is a punishment that came with disobedience
options.d: Only religious service pleases God; nothing else does

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-04.question: What sequence reveals the path of Eden through the Bible's story?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-04.learningObjective: See Eden as the start of a thread running through the Bible.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-04.feedbackCorrect: The lost garden becomes a promise and, at the end, God's servants serve him at the throne.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: garden (Gen 2), exile (Gen 3), promise (Isa 51) and city (Rev 22).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-04.hint: Start in the garden and end in the Bible's last book.

options.a: God places the man in the garden he planted
options.b: The man is sent out of Eden
options.c: God promises to make the desert like Eden
options.d: In God's city, his servants will serve him

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-05.question: In Genesis 2:15, which verb shows that work in the garden includes protecting it?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the sense of care.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-05.feedbackCorrect: To keep is to guard: the man makes sure the garden stays good, not exploits it.

feedbackWrong.a: The garden is not the man's property; he receives it to care for it.
feedbackWrong.b: The verse does not speak of dominating the garden; it speaks of working and protecting it.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-05.hint: It is the second verb of the task, next to working it.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-06.question: What links Genesis 2:10 to Revelation 22:1?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-06.learningObjective: Connect the river of Eden to the river of life in the new creation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-06.feedbackCorrect: The river that watered Eden reappears at the end, flowing from God's throne.

feedbackWrong.a: The river does not divide: it waters the garden and, at the end, flows from God's throne.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text speaks of judgment by water; both speak of life.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-05-eden-06.hint: Compare where the river flows from in each text.

options.a: The border between heaven and earth
options.b: The river of life restored
options.c: A new flood upon the earth

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-01.question: In Genesis 3:6, the woman gives some of the fruit to her husband, who was with her.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-01.learningObjective: Observe that the husband was with the woman and also ate.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-01.feedbackCorrect: The text records it: her husband was with her, and he ate too.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 3:6: she gave to her husband who was with her, and he ate.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-02.question: In Genesis 3:5, tap what the serpent says would be opened.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-02.learningObjective: Observe the promise the serpent makes.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-02.feedbackCorrect: The serpent promises opened eyes, as if God were hiding something from them.

feedbackWrong.a: "No dia" marks when, not what would be opened.
feedbackWrong.c: "O bem" is what she says they would know, not what would be opened.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-02.hint: See what the serpent promises would change in them.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-03.question: According to Genesis 3:2–3, what does the woman say about the trees of the garden?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-03.learningObjective: Observe the woman's answer to the serpent.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-03.feedbackCorrect: She corrects the serpent: they may eat from the trees; only the one in the middle is forbidden.

feedbackWrong.a: It is the opposite: the tree in the middle is the one they may not eat from.
feedbackWrong.b: She herself names an exception: the tree in the middle of the garden.
feedbackWrong.c: That is the serpent's insinuation; the woman answers that they may eat from the trees.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-03.hint: Read both verses: what is allowed and what is not.

options.a: They may eat only from the tree in the middle
options.b: They may eat from all of them, with no exception
options.c: They may not eat from any tree in the garden
options.d: They may eat from all but the one in the middle

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-04.question: Put the opening of Genesis 3:6 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of the woman's look in Genesis 3:6.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-04.feedbackCorrect: The woman's gaze builds: food, beauty and, finally, desire for understanding.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with what she saw first, good for food; understanding comes last.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-04.hint: The verse begins with what the woman saw.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-05.question: In Genesis 3:4, what does the serpent assure will not happen?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-05.feedbackCorrect: The serpent denies God's very warning: "you will surely die" (2:17).

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent does not speak of sin; it denies the death God announced.
feedbackWrong.b: The warning it contradicts is about death (2:17), not suffering.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-06.question: What does Genesis 3:1 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-06.learningObjective: Connect the serpent's question to the freedom God had given.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-06.feedbackCorrect: God gave wide freedom and only one limit; the question makes it seem the opposite.

feedbackWrong.a: God said "you may freely eat of every tree" (2:16); the question twists that.
feedbackWrong.b: Not at all: only one tree was forbidden (2:17), and the rest were free.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-06-queda-06.hint: Compare the question with what God said in 2:16.

options.a: It repeats God exactly
options.b: It confirms everything was forbidden
options.c: It distorts what God said

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-01.question: In Genesis 3:5, the serpent says God forbade the tree to protect the man and the woman.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-01.learningObjective: Understand how the serpent distorts God's motive.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-01.feedbackCorrect: For the serpent, God is not protecting: he "knows" of something good and is hiding it.

feedbackWrong.true: The serpent gives another motive: "Deus sabe" their eyes would open. It accuses God.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-01.hint: See the motive the serpent attributes to God.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-02.question: In Genesis 3:6, tap the action where the woman's desire becomes a deed.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-02.learningObjective: Recognize the moment the scene turns in Genesis 3:6.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-02.feedbackCorrect: She saw, desired and took: looking turns into action.

feedbackWrong.b: "Viu" is the beginning: still looking, not acting.
feedbackWrong.c: "Desejável" describes what she felt; the deed comes after.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-02.hint: Look for where seeing turns into a movement of the hands.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-03.question: How does the serpent's statement in Genesis 3:4 relate to God's warning in 2:17?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-03.learningObjective: Relate the serpent's words to God's word.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-03.feedbackCorrect: God said "you will surely die"; the serpent says "you will surely not die".

feedbackWrong.b: It does not explain: it contradicts, saying the opposite of what God said.
feedbackWrong.c: There is no middle ground: it claims they will not die.
feedbackWrong.d: It confirms nothing; it says the opposite of God's warning.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-03.hint: Set the two statements about dying side by side.

options.a: It denies God's warning, turning his words around
options.b: It explains God's warning in more detail
options.c: It softens the warning without denying death
options.d: It confirms the warning to win her trust

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-04.question: How is the woman's answer in Genesis 3:2–3 organized?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-04.learningObjective: Understand how the woman answers the serpent.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-04.feedbackCorrect: She starts with what is allowed, points out the exception and recalls God's warning.

feedbackWrong.default: First what they may eat (3:2); the exception and the warning come in 3:3.

options.a: The woman states what they may eat
options.b: She points to the tree in the middle of the garden
options.c: She repeats the warning of death

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-05.question: In Genesis 2:16, how does God say the man could eat from the trees of the garden?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-05.learningObjective: Understand the generosity of the command the serpent distorts.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-05.feedbackCorrect: God's command begins with generosity, not with prohibition.

feedbackWrong.a: Nothing is hidden: God speaks openly and gives every tree.
feedbackWrong.c: God does not limit how often: he gives every tree, with only one exception.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-05.hint: Compare with the serpent's question in 3:1.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-06.question: What links Genesis 3:6 to James 1:15?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-06.learningObjective: Relate the path of desire in Genesis and in James.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-06.feedbackCorrect: James describes what Genesis narrates: desire conceives and gives birth to sin.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, this desire turns against God's word.
feedbackWrong.b: James says sin brings death, as God warned in 2:17.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-06-queda-06.hint: Follow the path from desire to deed in both texts.

options.a: A desire God approves
options.b: Sin without consequence
options.c: Desire that leads to sin

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-01.question: In Genesis 3:6, the wrong is not in the fruit itself, which was good to eat, but in disobeying God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-01.learningObjective: Interpret the fall as disobedience, not a flaw in the fruit.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-01.feedbackCorrect: The tree was good, like all creation; the wrong was distrusting God and disobeying.

feedbackWrong.false: The text calls the tree good for food; the problem is the disobeyed command.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-01.hint: See how the verse describes the tree.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-02.question: In Genesis 3:5, tap the phrase that shows the serpent offering God's place.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that the temptation offers God's place.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-02.feedbackCorrect: The temptation is wanting God's place instead of trusting him.

feedbackWrong.a: "Se abrirão" promises opened eyes; the bigger ambition comes at the end of the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: "No dia" marks the time, not the offer.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-02.hint: Look for the comparison at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-03.question: What reading does Genesis 3:6 support about who disobeyed?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about both people's responsibility.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-03.feedbackCorrect: She eats and gives to her husband, who was with her; he eats too. Both disobey.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the husband was with her and also ate.
feedbackWrong.c: The serpent deceives, but the woman and her husband are the ones who take and eat.
feedbackWrong.d: The text says nothing of force: she gave, and he ate.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-03.hint: Read to the end of the verse and see who eats.

options.a: Only the woman is responsible; the man was not even there
options.b: Both disobey: she eats, and her husband does too
options.c: The blame is the serpent's alone, not theirs
options.d: The man is forced by the woman to eat

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-04.question: What sequence reveals what the disobedience of Genesis 3:6 sets in motion?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-04.learningObjective: See Genesis 3:6 as the start of a thread Paul connects to Christ.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-04.feedbackCorrect: Disobedience in the garden brings sin and death; in Christ comes resurrection.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow Paul: the fall (Gen 3:6), sin in the world (Rom 5:12) and life in Christ (1 Cor 15:22).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-04.hint: End with God's answer in Christ.

options.a: The man and the woman eat the forbidden fruit
options.b: Through one man, sin enters the world
options.c: In Christ, all will be raised

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-05.question: In Genesis 2:17, which word shows how firm God's warning is?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows the firmness of God's word.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-05.feedbackCorrect: God speaks firmly; the serpent copies the formula to deny it: "É certo que não".

feedbackWrong.b: The text marks the certainty of the warning, not the speed of death.
feedbackWrong.c: God's warning leaves no doubt; "maybe" is the tone the serpent would like.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-05.hint: Compare with the serpent's "É certo" in 3:4.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-06.question: What links Genesis 3:4 to Matthew 4:4?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-06.learningObjective: Connect the temptation in the garden to Jesus' victory by God's word.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-06.feedbackCorrect: In the garden, God's word is challenged; in the desert, Jesus stands firm on it.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus does not argue: he answers with what God said.
feedbackWrong.c: The point is not food, but which word one trusts.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-06-queda-06.hint: See what Jesus relies on when facing the tempter.

options.a: Trusting what God said
options.b: Arguing with the tempter
options.c: Avoiding all kinds of food

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-01.question: In Genesis 3:17, God declares the man himself cursed for eating from the tree.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-01.learningObjective: Observe that, in 3:17, the curse falls on the ground, because of the man.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-01.feedbackCorrect: What is called cursed is the ground, because of the man, not the man himself.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the middle of 3:17: "maldita é a terra por sua causa". The curse falls on the ground.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-01.hint: Find the word "maldita" and see what it refers to.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-02.question: In Genesis 3:14, tap whom the Lord God addresses with the first sentence.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-02.learningObjective: Identify the serpent as the first to receive a sentence.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-02.feedbackCorrect: The first sentence goes to the serpent, which deceived the woman (3:13).

feedbackWrong.a: The Lord God is the one speaking; the question is whom he addresses.
feedbackWrong.c: The livestock serve as a comparison: it is cursed among them.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-02.hint: See whom God speaks to at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-03.question: According to Genesis 3:14, how will the serpent move from now on?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-03.learningObjective: Observe the sentence given to the serpent.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-03.feedbackCorrect: The sentence is concrete: the serpent will crawl on its belly and eat dust.

feedbackWrong.a: The couple is the one sent out of Eden (3:23); God tells the serpent how it will move.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of trapping the serpent; it says it will crawl on its belly.
feedbackWrong.c: Adam and the woman were the ones who hid among the trees (3:8).

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-03.hint: Look for the verb of movement in the verse.

options.a: Fleeing far away from Eden
options.b: Trapped at the foot of the forbidden tree
options.c: Hidden among the trees of the garden
options.d: Crawling on its belly

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-04.question: Put Genesis 3:19 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: work with sweat, return to the ground, and the reason, dust.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with sweat and ends with "ao pó tornarás".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-05.question: In Genesis 3:18, what will the ground now produce along with thistles?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-05.learningObjective: Remember how the ground begins to resist human work.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-05.feedbackCorrect: Thorns and thistles: the ground that gave fruit now resists those who work it.

feedbackWrong.a: Before, the ground gave fruit freely; here it produces what hurts and hinders.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of flowers; it speaks of plants that make work hard.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-05.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-06.question: What does Genesis 3:19 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-06.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 3:19 to the warning of death in Genesis 2:17.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-06.feedbackCorrect: Returning to dust is dying: the warning of Genesis 2:17 comes true in human life.

feedbackWrong.a: It is not just humility: "ao pó tornarás" announces the end of life.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of death, not contempt for the body God formed.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-07-consequencias-06.hint: Compare where the man came from with where he is going.

options.a: Dust is only a sign of humility
options.b: Death enters human life
options.c: The human body has no worth

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-01.question: In Genesis 3:14, the serpent's sentence is presented as a response to what it did.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-01.learningObjective: Understand that the serpent's sentence is a consequence of what it did.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-01.feedbackCorrect: "Visto que fizeste isso": the sentence has a reason, the deception the serpent caused.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start: "Visto que fizeste isso" ties the sentence to what it did.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-01.hint: See how God begins speaking to the serpent.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-02.question: In Genesis 3:17, tap the words that link the curse on the ground to the man.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause link between the man's sin and the cursed ground.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-02.feedbackCorrect: "Por sua causa": the ground suffers because of what the man did.

feedbackWrong.a: "Sustento" is what he will get from the ground, not the reason for the curse.
feedbackWrong.b: "Fadigas" is the result of the curse, not what links it to the man.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-02.hint: Look for the phrase that says on whose account the ground suffers.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-03.question: In Genesis 3:15, how do the blow to the head and the blow to the heel relate?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-03.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the two wounds announced in 3:15.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-03.feedbackCorrect: Head against heel: both sides suffer, but the fatal blow falls on the serpent.

feedbackWrong.a: A wounded heel hurts; a wounded head means defeat. The weight is on the head.
feedbackWrong.c: The serpent strikes but does not win: the woman's offspring crushes its head.
feedbackWrong.d: The text speaks of no draw: striking the head is worse than striking the heel.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-03.hint: Compare the body part struck on each side.

options.a: The blow to the heel is the worse of the two
options.b: Both strike, but the decisive blow falls on the serpent
options.c: The serpent wins, and the woman is left defenseless
options.d: Both sides come out of the fight equally defeated

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-04.question: How do the sentences of Genesis 3:16–17 link together?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-04.learningObjective: Understand how the fall affects the body, relationships and work.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-04.feedbackCorrect: First the woman's pain and wounded relationship; then the ground, because of the man.

feedbackWrong.default: 3:16 speaks to the woman (pain and relationship); 3:17 turns to the man and the ground.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-04.hint: God speaks first to the woman, then to the man.

options.a: The woman will suffer pain in bearing children
options.b: The woman's relationship with her husband is wounded
options.c: The ground is cursed because of the man

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-05.question: In Genesis 3:15, which verb shows who establishes the hostility?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-05.learningObjective: Understand that God is the one who takes a stand against the serpent.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-05.feedbackCorrect: God is the one who puts the hostility in place: he himself takes a stand against the serpent.

feedbackWrong.a: God is not just a spectator of the fight: he is the one who sets it up.
feedbackWrong.b: God does not remove the hostility; he himself sets it against the serpent.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-05.hint: It is a first-person verb: God is the one speaking.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-06.question: What links Genesis 3:17 to Romans 8:20?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-06.learningObjective: Relate the cursed ground to the suffering creation of Romans 8.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul sees creation bound to futility, through no fault of its own: an echo of the cursed ground.

feedbackWrong.b: God made everything good (Gen 1:31); the ground suffers later, because of the man.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts creation suffers; it is not the one dealing out punishment.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-07-consequencias-06.hint: See what Paul says about creation's own will.
