options.a: Creation suffers from the fall
options.b: The earth was born flawed
options.c: Nature punishes humanity

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-01.question: Genesis 3:16 presents the husband's rule over the wife as God's ideal for the couple.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-01.learningObjective: Interpret 3:16 as describing the rupture caused by sin, not an ideal.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-01.feedbackCorrect: The verse describes what sin broke; creation's plan was "one flesh" (Gen 2:24).

feedbackWrong.true: 3:16 is among the consequences of the fall: it shows a wounded relationship, not the original design.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-01.hint: See where in the story this verse falls.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-02.question: In Genesis 3:15, tap the phrase that shows the serpent will not have the last word.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-02.learningObjective: Show from the text that 3:15 promises victory over the serpent.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-02.feedbackCorrect: Striking the head means defeat: the serpent strikes, but the woman's offspring will overcome it.

feedbackWrong.a: The hostility announces the fight; the outcome comes in the blow to the head.
feedbackWrong.b: The wounded heel shows there will be pain, but it is not the serpent's defeat.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-02.hint: Look for the blow that decides the fight.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-03.question: What reading does Genesis 3:14–15 support about the serpent's sentence?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading that sees promise within judgment.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-03.feedbackCorrect: Within the sentence itself is a promise: the woman's offspring will strike the serpent.

feedbackWrong.a: There is a winner: the wounded head is the serpent's.
feedbackWrong.b: Hope appears right there: the woman's offspring will strike the serpent.
feedbackWrong.d: God puts hostility, not peace, between the serpent and the woman.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-03.hint: Look for what God announces about the serpent's future.

options.a: The fight between good and evil will last forever, with no winner
options.b: God only punishes and leaves humans no hope
options.c: Even in judgment, God announces that evil will be defeated
options.d: The serpent and humanity will end up reconciled

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-04.question: What sequence reveals the path of the promise in Genesis 3:15?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-04.learningObjective: See Genesis 3:15 as the start of a promise the Bible follows to Christ.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-04.feedbackCorrect: The promise in Eden points to Jesus: born of a woman, he defeats the devil by his death.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: promise (Gen 3:15), birth (Gal 4:4), victory on the cross (Heb 2:14).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-04.hint: Start with the promise and end with the victory.

options.a: God promises an offspring of the woman who will strike the serpent
options.b: The Son of God is born of a woman
options.c: By his death, the Son defeats the one who held the power of death

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-05.question: In Genesis 3:15, who will strike the serpent's head?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the promise of 3:15.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-05.feedbackCorrect: The text moves from "descendência" to "o descendente": one from the woman will defeat the serpent.

feedbackWrong.a: The husband was already in the scene; the promise points to someone who will come from the woman.
feedbackWrong.b: The verse moves from the group ("descendência") to one person, who strikes the head.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-05.hint: See who, coming from the woman, strikes the head.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-06.question: What links Genesis 3:15 to Romans 16:20?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-06.learningObjective: Connect the promise of 3:15 to the final victory over evil announced in the NT.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul echoes Genesis: the enemy will be crushed underfoot, like the wounded serpent.

feedbackWrong.b: Paul reads the victory as Satan's defeat, not just an animal's.
feedbackWrong.c: There is no draw: the serpent's head is struck, and the God of peace crushes Satan.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-07-consequencias-06.hint: Compare where the serpent is struck and where Satan is crushed.

options.a: The promised victory over evil
options.b: The serpent was just an animal
options.c: Evil ties with God

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-01.question: In Genesis 4:3–4, Cain was the one who brought the Lord the firstborn of the flock.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-01.learningObjective: Observe what each brother offered the Lord.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-01.feedbackCorrect: Cain brought fruit of the ground; Abel was the one who brought the firstborn of the flock.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 4:4: "Abel também trouxe das primícias de seu rebanho".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-02.question: In Genesis 4:8, tap the place Cain called his brother to.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-02.learningObjective: Observe where the first murder happens.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-02.feedbackCorrect: Cain calls Abel to the field, and there he rises up against his brother.

feedbackWrong.a: Abel is the one who was called; the question is where to.
feedbackWrong.b: "Irmão" says who Abel was to Cain, not the place.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-02.hint: Look for a place within Cain's words.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-03.question: According to Genesis 4:5, how did Cain react when the Lord was not pleased with his offering?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-03.learningObjective: Observe Cain's reaction to the rejection of his offering.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-03.feedbackCorrect: The text records Cain's anger and fallen face: what he feels shows on the outside.

feedbackWrong.a: The text shows no repentance; it shows anger.
feedbackWrong.c: Cain does not accuse Abel here; the text speaks of his anger and his face.
feedbackWrong.d: Going to Nod only comes after the crime (4:16).

options.a: He asked forgiveness and brought another offering
options.b: He was very angry, and his face fell
options.c: He blamed Abel before the Lord
options.d: He left at once for the land of Nod

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-04.question: Put Genesis 4:8 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-04.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence of the first murder.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-04.feedbackCorrect: The verse moves from the invitation to the field, and from the field to the crime.

feedbackWrong.default: The invitation comes first; the attack closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-04.hint: The verse begins with Cain speaking.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-05.question: In Genesis 4:10, what cries out to God from the ground?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-05.learningObjective: Remember that God hears the victim's cry.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-05.feedbackCorrect: Abel's blood "has a voice": the violence done in the field reaches God.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of the body, but of what was shed on the ground.
feedbackWrong.b: There is no grave in the scene; what cries out comes from the ground where Abel fell.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-05.hint: See what has a voice in the verse's second sentence.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-06.question: What does Genesis 4:9 communicate that connects to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-06.learningObjective: Connect God's question to the crime Cain was trying to hide.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-06.feedbackCorrect: Cain acted in the field, but God comes right away to ask: nothing is hidden from him.

feedbackWrong.b: God asks to call Cain to answer; he then says the blood cries out (4:10).
feedbackWrong.c: Abel did not run away: Cain killed him in the field (4:8).

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-08-caim-06.hint: Think of what Cain had just done.

options.a: Nothing is hidden from God
options.b: God did not know where Abel was
options.c: Abel had run away from Cain

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-01.question: In Genesis 4:7, God shows Cain that he can still choose between doing right and doing wrong.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the two paths God presents.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-01.feedbackCorrect: God sets two paths before Cain: do what is right, or let sin come in.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread 4:7: "Se você agir corretamente... Mas, se agir mal". Both paths are open.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-01.hint: Notice the two "se" in the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-02.question: In Genesis 4:4–5, tap the word that marks the contrast between God's response to Abel and to Cain.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-02.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast between the two offerings.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-02.feedbackCorrect: "Mas" turns the scene: God is pleased with Abel, not with Cain and his offering.

feedbackWrong.b: "Também" adds: Abel also brought an offering. The contrast comes later.
feedbackWrong.c: "Sobremaneira" measures Cain's anger; the contrast comes earlier.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-02.hint: See the word linking the end of 4:4 to what follows.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-03.question: In Genesis 4:6–7, how do God's questions relate to Cain's anger?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-03.learningObjective: Understand that God confronts Cain before the crime, offering a way out.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-03.feedbackCorrect: Before the crime, God asks and warns: there is still time to do what is right.

feedbackWrong.a: God asks "Why are you angry?": he questions the anger, he does not approve it.
feedbackWrong.b: God does not compare the offerings' value; he speaks of what Cain must do now.
feedbackWrong.c: There is a way out: "If you do what is right, will you not be accepted?"

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-03.hint: See whether God speaks before or after Cain acts.

options.a: God approves Cain's anger as just
options.b: God explains that Abel's offering was worth more
options.c: God condemns him without giving any way out
options.d: God warns him in time to do what is right

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-04.question: How does the dialogue move in Genesis 4:9–10?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of confrontation in 4:9–10.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-04.feedbackCorrect: God asks, Cain dodges, and God shows he already knows: the blood cries out.

feedbackWrong.default: God's question opens the dialogue; the cry of the blood closes the passage.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-04.hint: The dialogue begins with a question from God.

options.a: God asks about Cain's brother
options.b: Cain denies knowing and dodges responsibility
options.c: God reveals that Abel's blood cries out to him

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-05.question: In Genesis 4:8, which verb shows Cain moving to attack his brother?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-05.learningObjective: Understand the step from anger to violence.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-05.feedbackCorrect: The anger God told him to master becomes an attack: Cain rises against his brother.

feedbackWrong.a: Cain does more than complain: he attacks and kills his brother.
feedbackWrong.b: The anger came earlier (4:5); here it has already become action against Abel.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-05.hint: Look for the action right after "enquanto estavam no campo".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-06.question: What links Genesis 4:5 to 1 John 3:15?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-06.learningObjective: Relate Cain's anger to John's teaching on hatred.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-06.feedbackCorrect: John shows what Cain reveals: hatred of a brother already carries the seed of murder.

feedbackWrong.a: In Cain, unmastered anger ended in death (4:8).
feedbackWrong.b: John says the opposite: hating a brother already makes one a murderer, before any act.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-08-caim-06.hint: Compare what Cain feels with what John says about whoever hates.

options.a: Anger never has consequences
options.b: What we feel does not matter
options.c: From hatred to murder

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-01.question: Genesis 4:4–5 explains that God rejected Cain's offering because it was plants, not animals.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-01.learningObjective: Interpret the rejection without going beyond what the text and the NT say.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-01.feedbackCorrect: The text gives no such reason. Hebrews 11:4 speaks of Abel's faith; 1 John 3:12, of Cain's deeds.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 4:4–5: the text says God was not pleased, but not that it was due to the kind of offering.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-01.hint: Check whether the text says why it was rejected.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-02.question: In Genesis 4:7, tap the phrase that shows sin as a threat very close to Cain.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-02.learningObjective: Support from the text the image of sin as a nearby threat.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-02.feedbackCorrect: Sin crouches at the door, ready to master whoever does not master it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Será aceito" is the promise for those who do well, not the threat.
feedbackWrong.b: "Agir corretamente" is the opposite path; the threat comes in the second half.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-02.hint: Look for where sin is found, in the second half of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-03.question: What reading does Genesis 4:10 support about God's question to Cain?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading that sees God's question as a call to responsibility.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-03.feedbackCorrect: God hears the blood crying out: he knows, and he asks so that Cain will answer.

feedbackWrong.a: God himself says Abel's blood cries out to him: nothing escaped him.
feedbackWrong.b: The question "Onde está Abel, teu irmão?" shows Cain was answerable for his brother.
feedbackWrong.d: "O que fizeste?" calls him to account; the sentence follows (4:11–12).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-03.hint: See what God says reaches him.

options.a: God did not know what had happened in the field
options.b: Each one answers only for himself, not for his brother
options.c: God already knows what happened and calls Cain to answer
options.d: God only records the fact, without holding anyone to account

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of Abel's blood through the Bible?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-04.learningObjective: See the cry of Abel's blood as a thread that leads to the blood of Jesus.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-04.feedbackCorrect: The blood that cries for justice points to the blood of Jesus, which speaks a better word.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: Genesis 4:10, then Jesus (Matt 23:35) and finally Hebrews 12:24.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-04.hint: Follow the order of the biblical story: Genesis, Gospels, Hebrews.

options.a: Abel's blood cries out to God from the ground
options.b: Jesus recalls the blood of righteous Abel
options.c: Jesus' blood speaks better than Abel's

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-05.question: In Genesis 4:9, what does Cain call the role he denies having toward his brother?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries responsibility for the other.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-05.feedbackCorrect: Cain denies being a keeper, but God's question shows he was answerable for his brother.

feedbackWrong.a: Cain does not speak of ruling his brother; he speaks of caring for him, and denies that role.
feedbackWrong.b: Cain does not speak of judging; he denies the role of caring for his brother.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-05.hint: Look at Cain's answer at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-06.question: What links Genesis 4:4 to Hebrews 11:4?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-06.learningObjective: Link Abel's approval to faith, as Hebrews does.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews says what Genesis does not explain: Abel offered by faith, and God was pleased.

feedbackWrong.a: Hebrews speaks not of cost but of faith: "By faith Abel offered".
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not tie approval to age; Hebrews points to Abel's faith.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-08-caim-06.hint: Look at the phrase that opens Hebrews 11:4.

options.a: The higher cost of the offering
options.b: The faith behind the offering
options.c: A preference for the younger brother

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-01.question: In Genesis 6:5, the Lord saw that human wickedness was multiplying on the earth.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-01.learningObjective: Observe that God sees the wickedness growing on the earth.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says the Lord saw human wickedness multiplying on the earth.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Genesis 6:5: the Lord saw that wickedness was multiplying.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-01.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-02.question: In Genesis 6:8–9, tap what Noah found before the Lord.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-02.learningObjective: Identify the grace Noah receives from the Lord.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-02.feedbackCorrect: Noah found grace: the favor comes from the Lord, amid a corrupt generation.

feedbackWrong.a: "Justo" describes Noah in 6:9; what he found before the Lord comes earlier.
feedbackWrong.c: "Gerações" opens the story of Noah's family, not what he found.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-02.hint: Look for what comes right after "encontrou".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-03.question: According to Genesis 9:12, with whom does God establish the covenant?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-03.learningObjective: Observe the reach of the covenant made after the flood.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-03.feedbackCorrect: The covenant is "entre mim e vocês, e entre todos os seres vivos": people and animals.

feedbackWrong.b: God speaks to "vocês" and includes every living creature; it is not only Noah.
feedbackWrong.c: The animals are included, but the covenant is also with Noah and his family.
feedbackWrong.d: "Para gerações eternas" says how long it lasts, not that it leaves out those present.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-03.hint: Look at every "entre" in the verse.

options.a: With Noah and his family, and with every living creature
options.b: Only with Noah, the righteous man
options.c: Only with the animals that were on the ark
options.d: Only with future generations

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-04.question: Put Genesis 6:9 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's sequence: Noah's family, his character and his life with God.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with Noah's generations; life with God closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-04.hint: The verse begins by introducing a family.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-05.question: In Genesis 9:13, what did God set in the clouds?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-05.learningObjective: Remember the visible sign of the covenant.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-05.feedbackCorrect: God sets his bow in the clouds: a sign anyone can see after the rain.

feedbackWrong.b: God does not write a name in the sky; he places a visible sign there.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of a seal; it speaks of something that appears in the clouds.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-05.hint: Think of what appears in the sky after the rain.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-06.question: What does Genesis 6:7 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-06.learningObjective: Link the announcement of judgment to the wickedness God saw.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-06.feedbackCorrect: The announcement in 6:7 answers what God saw in 6:5: the wickedness ruling the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: God does not ignore it: he sees the wickedness and responds to it.
feedbackWrong.c: The text gives the reason: human wickedness, seen by God in 6:5.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-09-diluvio-06.hint: Remember what the Lord saw in verse 5.

options.a: God ignores violence
options.b: God judges human wickedness
options.c: God destroys for no reason

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-01.question: In Genesis 9:12–13, the bow is the sign of a covenant that depends on Noah obeying.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-01.learningObjective: Understand that the bow points to God's commitment.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-01.feedbackCorrect: The bow is the sign of the covenant God establishes: the initiative and commitment are his.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 9:12: "a minha aliança que estabeleço". God sets no condition on Noah here.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-02.question: In Genesis 6:8, tap the word that marks the turn after the announcement of judgment.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-02.learningObjective: Recognize the marker of contrast between judgment and grace.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-02.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" turns the scene: God announces judgment, but Noah finds grace.

feedbackWrong.a: "Encontrou" says what Noah received; the turn comes earlier, right after his name.
feedbackWrong.c: "Diante" shows where Noah stands, not the contrast with 6:7.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-02.hint: It is a short word, right after Noah's name.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-03.question: How does Genesis 6:8 relate to the announcement in Genesis 6:7?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-03.learningObjective: Relate the announcement of judgment to the grace given to Noah.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-03.feedbackCorrect: The judgment still stands, but Noah finds grace: there is a way out within the sentence.

feedbackWrong.a: The judgment is not canceled; the flood comes. Grace reaches Noah in the midst of it.
feedbackWrong.b: Noah says nothing here; grace comes from the Lord, not from a request of his.
feedbackWrong.d: Verse 8 does not repeat the judgment; it changes course with "porém".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-03.hint: Think about what "porém" does between the two verses.

options.a: It cancels the judgment God had just announced
options.b: It shows Noah convinced God to change his mind
options.c: It opens an exception of grace within the announced judgment
options.d: It repeats the announcement of judgment in other words

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-04.question: How does the scene move in Genesis 6:5–6?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from God's seeing to his grief.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-04.feedbackCorrect: God sees the evil, sees it rules the human heart, and feels its weight.

feedbackWrong.default: The weight on God's heart comes last: before that, he sees the evil and its reach.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-04.hint: The "Então" in verse 6 shows what comes next.

options.a: The Lord sees wickedness spreading over the earth
options.b: Evil rules even human thoughts
options.c: The wickedness weighs on God's own heart

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-05.question: In Genesis 6:7, which word introduces the reason God gives for the judgment?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-05.learningObjective: Understand the link between God's decision and its reason.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-05.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" introduces the reason: God speaks of the grief of making those given over to evil.

feedbackWrong.b: "Quando" would speak of time; the text is giving a reason.
feedbackWrong.c: "Mas" would set up a contrast; here the end of the verse explains the decision.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-05.hint: The word links the announcement to the reason, at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-06.question: What links Genesis 6:9 to Hebrews 11:7?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-06.learningObjective: Relate Noah's life to the faith described in Hebrews.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews shows what that walk with God was like: Noah trusted what God said and acted.

feedbackWrong.b: Hebrews says "by faith" and speaks of Noah "warned by God": it is not his own effort.
feedbackWrong.c: Noah foresaw nothing on his own; God warned him about things not yet seen.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-09-diluvio-06.hint: See how Hebrews begins the sentence about Noah.

options.a: Walking with God by faith
options.b: Saving oneself by one's own effort
options.c: Predicting the future without God

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-01.question: In Genesis 6:5–6, the Lord's regret appears as grief over human evil, not as a mistake by God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-01.learningObjective: Interpret God's regret as grief over sin.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-01.feedbackCorrect: The problem named is human wickedness (6:5); what God feels is grief: "isso lhe pesou".

feedbackWrong.false: The text does not speak of a mistake by God; it speaks of human evil and the weight it lays on God.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-01.hint: Compare what the Lord sees with what he feels.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-02.question: In Genesis 6:5, tap the word that shows evil goes beyond actions, down to the inner life.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that sin reaches the human inner life.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-02.feedbackCorrect: Evil is in the heart: it is born inside, before it becomes violence outside.

feedbackWrong.b: The earth is where wickedness spreads, not where it is born.
feedbackWrong.c: "Maldade" names the problem; the text says where it lives further on.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-02.hint: Look for the part of the person where thoughts come from.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-03.question: What reading does Genesis 6:8–9 support about Noah?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about grace and righteousness in Noah.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-03.feedbackCorrect: The text names grace first (6:8); then it shows Noah living with God (6:9).

feedbackWrong.a: Before calling Noah righteous, the text says he found grace.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of payment: Noah finds grace before the Lord.
feedbackWrong.d: There is no chance here: Noah finds grace "diante do Senhor", and God goes on with creation.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-03.hint: Notice what comes first: grace or the description of Noah.

options.a: Noah's righteousness shows he did not need grace
options.b: Noah earned grace as payment for his righteousness
options.c: Grace comes from the Lord, and Noah responds by walking with God
options.d: God gave up on creation and saved Noah by chance

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-04.question: Which sequence reveals how the Bible returns to Noah's story?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-04.learningObjective: See the flood as a story the Bible returns to in order to teach.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-04.feedbackCorrect: The flood becomes a reference: Jesus uses it as a warning, and Peter as proof of judgment and care.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: Genesis (6:8), Jesus in the Gospels (Matt 24:37) and the letters (2 Pet 2:5).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, Gospels, letters.

options.a: Noah finds grace when God announces judgment
options.b: Jesus compares his coming to the days of Noah
options.c: Peter recalls that God preserved Noah and seven others

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-05.question: In Genesis 9:12, which term names the commitment the sign represents?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the theological meaning of the scene.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-05.feedbackCorrect: It is the covenant: God commits himself to Noah, to living creatures and to future generations.

feedbackWrong.a: The judgment is past; the sign points to the commitment God takes on.
feedbackWrong.c: The sign does not celebrate a victory; it points to a commitment by God.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-05.hint: See what the sign represents, according to God himself.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-06.question: What links Genesis 9:13 to Isaiah 54:9?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-06.learningObjective: Link the covenant of the bow to God's faithfulness proclaimed by the prophets.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-06.feedbackCorrect: Centuries later, Isaiah uses the promise to Noah as a guarantee of God's faithfulness.

feedbackWrong.a: Isaiah speaks of what God swore; the covenant's firmness rests in him, not in Noah.
feedbackWrong.b: The bow points to the opposite: the waters of Noah would never flood the earth again.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-09-diluvio-06.hint: See what Isaiah says God did about the waters of Noah.

options.a: The covenant depends on Noah
options.b: The bow announces another flood
options.c: God keeps what he swore

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-01.question: In Genesis 11:1, the peoples of the earth spoke many different languages.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-01.learningObjective: Observe that humanity begins the scene united by language.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-01.feedbackCorrect: Before Babel, the whole earth had one language and used the same words.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 11:1: the whole earth had a single language.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-01.hint: See how many languages the verse mentions.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-02.question: In Genesis 11:5, tap who was behind the building.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-02.feedbackCorrect: The builders are the "filhos dos homens": ordinary people trying to reach the heavens.

feedbackWrong.a: The Lord does not build; he comes to look at what others are building.
feedbackWrong.b: The tower is what was being built, not who was building.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-02.hint: Look for who does the building, at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-03.question: According to Genesis 11:2, where did the people settle after leaving the East?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-03.learningObjective: Observe where the Babel scene takes place.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-03.feedbackCorrect: The people reach a plain in Shinar and settle there, instead of filling the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: Eden was left behind in Genesis 3; the people settle in Shinar.
feedbackWrong.b: Ararat appears in the flood (Gen 8:4); here the people reach a plain.
feedbackWrong.c: Canaan will be Abram's destination (Gen 12:5); here the people live in Shinar.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: In the garden of Eden
options.b: In the mountains of Ararat
options.c: In the land of Canaan
options.d: On a plain in Shinar

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-04.question: Put Genesis 11:3 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: the decision, brick instead of stone, and tar as mortar.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the decision to make bricks; the tar closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-04.hint: The verse begins with an invitation.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-05.question: In Genesis 11:9, what name did the city receive?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-05.learningObjective: Remember the name of the city of the tower.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-05.feedbackCorrect: The city became known as Babel, tied to the language the Lord confused there.

feedbackWrong.a: Shinar is the region of the plain (11:2), not the city's name.
feedbackWrong.c: Nineveh is another city, mentioned in Genesis 10:11.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-05.hint: The name recalls what the Lord did with the language there.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-06.question: What does Genesis 11:8 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-06.learningObjective: Link Genesis 11:8 to the end of the Babel project.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-06.feedbackCorrect: "Cessaram de edificar": the great project stopped halfway.

feedbackWrong.b: The people were scattered and stopped building; the city was not finished.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not say the tower reached the heavens; it says the work stopped.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-10-babel-06.hint: See what happens to the building at the end of the verse.

options.a: The work was left unfinished
options.b: The people finished the city
options.c: The tower reached the heavens

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-01.question: In Genesis 11:4, fear of being scattered over the earth is part of the reason for building.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-01.learningObjective: Understand the purpose behind the building.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-01.feedbackCorrect: "Para que não sejamos espalhados": the tower is also a plan for their own security.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of 11:4: they build "para que não sejamos espalhados".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-01.hint: Look at the last part of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-02.question: In Genesis 11:9, tap the word that introduces the reason for the city's name.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-02.learningObjective: Recognize the marker of cause in the text.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-02.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" gives the reason: the city has this name because there the Lord confused the language.

feedbackWrong.a: "Toda" gives the reach of the confusion, not the reason for the name.
feedbackWrong.c: "Dali" shows where the peoples left from, not the reason for the name.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-02.hint: Look for the word right after the city's name.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-03.question: In Genesis 11:8, how does the outcome relate to the plan in Genesis 11:4?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-03.learningObjective: Relate the human plan to the outcome God brings.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-03.feedbackCorrect: They built so as not to be scattered (11:4), and the Lord scattered them (11:8).

feedbackWrong.a: It is the Lord who scatters them; it was not their choice.
feedbackWrong.b: The text says the opposite: the Lord scattered them over the face of the earth.
feedbackWrong.d: The work was not finished: "cessaram de edificar a cidade".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-03.hint: Compare the fear in 11:4 with what the Lord does in 11:8.

options.a: They scatter of their own will
options.b: The Lord gathers them for good in one city
options.c: Exactly what they wanted to avoid happens
options.d: They finish the tower and only then scatter

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-04.question: How does the scene move in Genesis 11:4–5?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the human project to God's coming.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-04.feedbackCorrect: First the project, then the motive behind it, and then the Lord comes to see the work.

feedbackWrong.default: The Lord's coming closes the scene: before it come the people's project and motive.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-04.hint: The "Então" in verse 5 shifts the focus of the scene.

options.a: The people decide to build a city and a tower
options.b: The people seek fame and security for themselves
options.c: The Lord comes to see the human work up close

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-05.question: In Genesis 11:7, what does God decide to do with the people's language?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-05.learningObjective: Understand the act of God that changes the scene.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-05.feedbackCorrect: God confuses the language, and the shared project stops: no one understands the other.

feedbackWrong.a: Hearing would not explain the result: "para que ninguém entenda a linguagem de outro".
feedbackWrong.b: Keeping the language would preserve unity; the end of the verse shows the opposite.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-05.hint: Read the result at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-06.question: What links Genesis 11:9 to Luke 1:51?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-06.learningObjective: Relate Babel to the way God deals with the proud.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-06.feedbackCorrect: Mary's song says what Babel already showed: God scatters those who exalt themselves.

feedbackWrong.a: In both texts, those who exalt themselves are scattered, not rewarded.
feedbackWrong.c: At Babel, pride ends in division, not unity.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-10-babel-06.hint: Compare the verb that appears in both texts.

options.a: God rewards those who exalt themselves
options.b: God scatters the proud
options.c: Pride unites the peoples

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-01.question: In Genesis 11:3–4, Babel's sin lies in using bricks and in building technique.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-01.learningObjective: Distinguish Babel's sin from a mistaken reading about technique.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-01.feedbackCorrect: The text points to the motive: making a name and not being scattered. Brick is not the issue.

feedbackWrong.true: The bricks are just material; the problem shows up in "façamos um nome para nós".

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-01.hint: Look for what they wanted to achieve with the work.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-02.question: In Genesis 11:5, tap the word that shows, with irony, that the tower stayed far from God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-02.learningObjective: Support from the text the distance between the tower and God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-02.feedbackCorrect: The tower was meant to reach the heavens, yet the Lord still has to come down to see it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Observar" says what the Lord does on arriving; the irony is in his movement.
feedbackWrong.c: "Edificando" is the people's action; the irony is in what the Lord does.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-02.hint: Look at the Lord's movement at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-03.question: What reading does Genesis 11:6–7 support about God's action at Babel?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about the judgment at Babel.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-03.feedbackCorrect: "Isso é apenas o início": God limits a project of pride before it grows.

feedbackWrong.b: The problem is not working together; it is working to make a name without God.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord had to come down to see the tower; the text does not show God threatened.
feedbackWrong.d: The scattering checks pride; later the Bible shows peoples gathered before God.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-03.hint: Read carefully what God says about the "início".

options.a: God checks human pride before it goes further
options.b: God condemns all work done together
options.c: God fears losing his place to humans
options.d: God wants the peoples isolated from each other forever

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of languages in the biblical story?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-04.learningObjective: See the division at Babel within God's plan to gather the peoples.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-04.feedbackCorrect: The languages divided at Babel are heard at Pentecost and gathered before the throne.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: Babel (Gen 11:9), Pentecost (Acts 2:6) and God's throne (Rev 7:9).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, Acts, Revelation.

options.a: At Babel, the Lord confuses the language of the whole earth
options.b: At Pentecost, each one hears in his own language
options.c: People of every language stand before the throne

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-05.question: In Genesis 11:4, which term shows what the people sought for themselves?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-05.feedbackCorrect: They want a name: fame and security built by themselves, without God.

feedbackWrong.a: The text speaks of a city and tower; they sought their own fame, not a place of worship.
feedbackWrong.b: They already had a place to live (11:2); what they sought was fame.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-05.hint: Look at what they wanted to do right after speaking of the tower.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-06.question: What links Genesis 11:4 to Genesis 12:2?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-06.learningObjective: Link Babel to Abram's call through the theme of the name.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-06.feedbackCorrect: At Babel the people want to make a name; soon after, God promises to make Abram's name great.

feedbackWrong.a: Abram builds no tower; he receives a promise from God.
feedbackWrong.b: In 12:2, the great name comes from God: he will make Abram's name great.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-10-babel-06.hint: See who makes the name grow in each text.

options.a: Abram also builds a tower
options.b: The name comes from human effort
options.c: God is the one who makes the name great

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-01.question: In Genesis 12:4, Lot went with Abram when he left.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says: Abram left, "e Ló o acompanhou".

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the middle of Genesis 12:4: "e Ló o acompanhou".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-01.hint: See who appears beside Abram in the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-02.question: In Genesis 12:1, tap who receives the command to leave.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-02.learningObjective: Identify to whom God addresses the call.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-02.feedbackCorrect: The command is addressed to him: "O Senhor disse a Abrão: Saia".

feedbackWrong.a: His father's house is what must be left; the father does not receive the command.
feedbackWrong.c: The Lord gives the command; he does not receive it.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-02.hint: See whom the Lord speaks to at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-03.question: According to Genesis 12:2, what does God promise to make of Abram?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-03.learningObjective: Observe the first promise made to Abram.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-03.feedbackCorrect: The first promise is "Farei de você uma grande nação", spoken to a childless man.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of a king here; it speaks of a great nation.
feedbackWrong.b: Building a city was Babel's plan; here God promises to make a nation.
feedbackWrong.c: There is no temple or priesthood in 12:2; the promise is a great nation.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-03.hint: Read the start of the verse.

options.a: A mighty king
options.b: A builder of cities
options.c: A priest of the temple
options.d: A great nation

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-04.question: Put Genesis 12:1 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: the land, the relatives, the father's house and finally the destination.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "Saia da sua terra"; the destination God will show closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-04.hint: The verse moves from the widest to the closest, and only then names the destination.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-05.question: In Genesis 12:4, where did Abram leave from?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-05.feedbackCorrect: Abram left Haran at seventy-five, where the family had stopped (11:31).

feedbackWrong.b: Shinar is the plain of Babel (11:2), not the place Abram leaves from.
feedbackWrong.c: Ur was the family's starting point (11:31); now Abram leaves another place.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-05.hint: See the place named at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-06.question: What does Genesis 12:5 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-06.learningObjective: Link Abram's departure to his arrival in Canaan.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-06.feedbackCorrect: The journey ends at its goal: "Partiram em direção à terra de Canaã e lá chegaram".

feedbackWrong.a: Abram leaves Haran (12:4) and reaches Canaan (12:5).
feedbackWrong.b: Abram does not turn back; he goes on toward Canaan.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-11-abraao-06.hint: See the destination named at the end of the verse.

options.a: Abram stays in Haran
options.b: Abram goes back to Ur
options.c: Abram reaches Canaan

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-01.question: In Genesis 12:1, God shows Abram the land before telling him to leave.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-01.learningObjective: Understand the order between the call and the destination.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-01.feedbackCorrect: The command to leave comes first; the land would be shown later: "que eu lhe mostrarei".

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of 12:1: "a terra que eu lhe mostrarei", still in the future.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-01.hint: Notice the verb tense at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-02.question: In Genesis 12:1, tap the first command the Lord gives Abram.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-02.learningObjective: Recognize the action that changes the scene.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-02.feedbackCorrect: "Saia" opens the call: before any promise, God asks Abram to leave something behind.

feedbackWrong.b: "Vá" comes later: first Abram has to leave.
feedbackWrong.c: "Mostrarei" is what God will do, not a command to Abram.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-02.hint: Look for the first verb addressed to Abram.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-03.question: How does Genesis 12:4 relate to the command in Genesis 12:1?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-03.learningObjective: Relate Abram's departure to God's command.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-03.feedbackCorrect: "Partiu, portanto": the departure is the direct response to the command in 12:1.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no bargaining: he leaves "conforme o que o SENHOR lhe ordenara".
feedbackWrong.c: Lot went with him, and the text soon names Sarai (12:5).
feedbackWrong.d: The land was yet to be shown; Abram leaves first, trusting.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-03.hint: Notice the word between commas at the very start of 12:4.

options.a: Abram does what the Lord had commanded
options.b: Abram bargains with God before leaving
options.c: Abram leaves alone, without any family
options.d: Abram leaves only after seeing the land

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-04.question: How does God's speech move in Genesis 12:1–2?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from command to promise.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-04.feedbackCorrect: God asks Abram to leave everything, points to a hidden destination, and only then promises.

feedbackWrong.default: The command to leave comes first; the promises begin in verse 2.

options.a: The command to leave what is familiar
options.b: The destination God will still show
options.c: The promise of a great nation

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-05.question: In Genesis 12:2, what does God promise to do with Abram's name?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-05.learningObjective: Understand God's action on Abram's name.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-05.feedbackCorrect: God himself makes Abram's name great, the very thing Babel tried to win on its own.

feedbackWrong.a: God does not erase Abram's name; he makes it great.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of keeping it: God makes the name grow.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-05.hint: Compare with what the people of Babel tried to do on their own.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-06.question: What links Genesis 12:4 to Hebrews 11:8?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-06.learningObjective: Relate Abram's departure to the faith described in Hebrews.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-06.feedbackCorrect: Hebrews explains the departure: Abraham obeyed by faith and went out not knowing where.

feedbackWrong.a: Hebrews speaks of faith and obedience, not ambition.
feedbackWrong.b: Hebrews says the opposite: he "went out, not knowing where he was going".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-11-abraao-06.hint: See how Hebrews describes Abraham's departure.

options.a: Leaving out of ambition
options.b: Leaving after seeing the land
options.c: Obeying by faith

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-01.question: Genesis 12:1–2 presents the call as God's initiative, not as a reward for any merit of Abram's.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-01.learningObjective: Interpret Abram's call as the initiative of God's grace.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-01.feedbackCorrect: The text opens with "O Senhor disse" and mentions nothing Abram had done before.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: the one who speaks and promises is the Lord; the text points to no merit in Abram.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-01.hint: See who starts the action and what the text says about Abram before that.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-02.question: In Genesis 12:3, tap the word that shows the promise leaves no people out.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-02.learningObjective: Support from the text the universal reach of the promise.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-02.feedbackCorrect: "Todas" the families of the earth: the promise reaches the peoples scattered at Babel.

feedbackWrong.a: "Você" points to Abram, through whom the blessing comes, not to its reach.
feedbackWrong.c: "Benditas" says what the families receive, not how many.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-02.hint: Look for the word that gives the reach of the promise.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-03.question: What reading does Genesis 12:2–3 support about the favor God gives Abram?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about the purpose of the blessing.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-03.feedbackCorrect: Abram receives in order to pass it on: through him, all families of the earth will be blessed.

feedbackWrong.a: The text opens the favor to all families of the earth, not just Abram's.
feedbackWrong.b: The great name is there, but the goal is to bless all families of the earth.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of reward; everything starts from God's word.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-03.hint: Read the end of 12:3 before choosing.

options.a: God's favor stays closed within Abram's family
options.b: What God promises comes down to wealth and fame
options.c: Abram is blessed so that other peoples will be too
options.d: God rewards Abram for his goodness

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-04.question: Which sequence reveals the fulfillment of the promise in Genesis 12:3?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-04.learningObjective: See Genesis 12:3 as a promise fulfilled in Christ.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-04.feedbackCorrect: The promise to Abram runs through Jesus, son of Abraham, and reaches the nations by faith.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: the promise (Gen 12:3), Jesus' birth (Matt 1:1) and the church (Gal 3:14).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, Gospels, letters.

options.a: God promises to bless all families in Abram
options.b: Jesus is born as the son of Abraham
options.c: Abraham's blessing reaches the Gentiles in Christ

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-05.question: In Genesis 12:2, what will Abram be for others, according to the end of the verse?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the theological meaning of the scene.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-05.feedbackCorrect: Abram does not only receive God's favor: he becomes a channel of that favor to others.

feedbackWrong.b: Abram is not just an example to watch; he carries God's favor to others.
feedbackWrong.c: Glory is not the focus: Abram receives in order to pass on what God gives.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-05.hint: Look at what God has just promised to do for Abram in the same verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-06.question: What links Genesis 12:3 to Galatians 3:8?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-06.learningObjective: Link the promise to Abram to the gospel, as Paul himself does.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul says Scripture announced the gospel to Abraham with this promise.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul reads the promise as good news for the Gentiles, not only for Israel.
feedbackWrong.c: Paul shows the promise alive, fulfilled in those who believe.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-11-abraao-06.hint: See what Paul says Scripture announced beforehand.

options.a: A blessing only for Israel
options.b: The gospel announced to Abraham
options.c: A promise long forgotten

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-01.question: In Genesis 1:16, besides the two great lights, God also made the stars.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-01.learningObjective: Observe that the heavenly bodies are God's work.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-01.feedbackCorrect: The text mentions the stars almost in passing: they too are God's work.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Genesis 1:16: "e também fez as estrelas".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:6, tap what God commands to be in the midst of the waters.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-02.learningObjective: Observe God's command on the second day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-02.feedbackCorrect: God commands an expanse in the midst of the waters: a space opened by his word.

feedbackWrong.a: The waters are already there; God commands something new in their midst.
feedbackWrong.b: "Separação" is the effect; what God commands to be in the waters comes first.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-02.hint: Read the command God gives at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-03.question: According to Genesis 1:10, what names does God give to the dry land and the gathered waters?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-03.learningObjective: Observe the names God gives on the third day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-03.feedbackCorrect: God names the dry land and the waters: Earth and Seas. The one who names is the one who rules.

feedbackWrong.a: Day and Night are the names of light and darkness (1:5).
feedbackWrong.b: The deep appears in 1:2; the gathered waters are named Seas.
feedbackWrong.d: Heavens is the name of the expanse (1:8); here it is the dry land and the waters.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-03.hint: Read the two names God gives in the verse.

options.a: Day and Night
options.b: Earth and Deep
options.c: Earth and Seas
options.d: Heavens and Earth

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-04.question: Put Genesis 1:31 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-04.feedbackCorrect: God looks at the work, gives the verdict "muito bom", and only then the day closes.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God looking at the work; the sixth day closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-04.hint: The verse begins with God looking.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:21, what great animals does God create, along with the birds?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-05.learningObjective: Remember what God creates on the fifth day.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-05.feedbackCorrect: Even the great sea creatures are creatures: God made them and saw that it was good.

feedbackWrong.a: Livestock only appear on the sixth day; 1:21 speaks of the sea and the birds.
feedbackWrong.b: Wild animals appear on the sixth day (1:24–25); here it is those of the sea.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-05.hint: Think of the waters of the fifth day.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-06.question: What does Genesis 1:14 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-06.learningObjective: Link Genesis 1:14 to God's care for time.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-06.feedbackCorrect: The lights mark days, seasons and years: time too is God's work.

feedbackWrong.a: The text gives time fixed markers: days, seasons and years.
feedbackWrong.b: The lights are signs of time, not of fate; God is the one who sets them in the sky.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-06.hint: See what the lights are for at the end of the verse.

options.a: Time runs without order
options.b: The stars decide our fate
options.c: God orders time

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-07.question: In Genesis 1:30, tap what God gives the animals as food.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-07.learningObjective: Observe that God provides food for the animals too.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-07.feedbackCorrect: To the animals God gives every green plant: he sustains what is not human, too.

feedbackWrong.a: "Fôlego de vida" is what the animals have, not what they get to eat.
feedbackWrong.c: The bird of the sky is among those who receive food; it is not the food.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-07.hint: Read the last part of God's speech.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-08.question: Put Genesis 1:20 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-08.feedbackCorrect: God speaks, and the command fills first the waters and then the sky with life.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with God's speech; the waters come before the birds.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-01-08.hint: The verse begins with who speaks.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-01.question: In Genesis 1:31, God repeats over the whole work the same verdict as on the other days, with nothing more.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between each day's good and the whole's very good.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-01.feedbackCorrect: On the other days God saw it was good; over the whole, the verdict rises: very good.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 1:31: it is not just "bom", as on the other days, but "muito bom".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-01.hint: Compare with the refrain of the earlier days.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:26, tap the word that links God's speech to what came before.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-02.learningObjective: Recognize the sequence marker before the creation of humankind.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-02.feedbackCorrect: "Então" marks the next step: after making the animals, God speaks of humankind.

feedbackWrong.b: "Façamos" is God's speech itself, not the link to what came before.
feedbackWrong.c: "Sobre" shows what humans will rule, not a link.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-02.hint: Look for the word that marks the next step of the story.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-03.question: How does Genesis 1:30 relate to Genesis 1:29?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-03.learningObjective: Relate God's care for humans and for animals.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-03.feedbackCorrect: After giving food to humans, God also provides for every creature with the breath of life.

feedbackWrong.a: In 1:29–30 no one is food for anyone; all receive plants.
feedbackWrong.b: God is the one who speaks and gives: "toda erva verde será para alimento".
feedbackWrong.d: Nothing is taken away: each one receives its food from God.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-03.hint: See who the food is for in each verse.

options.a: The animals become food for humans
options.b: The animals must find their own food, without God
options.c: God also gives food to the animals, not only to humans
options.d: God takes from the animals the food given to humans

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-04.question: How does the first day move in Genesis 1:4–5?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-04.learningObjective: Understand the movements of the first day.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-04.feedbackCorrect: God evaluates, separates and names: the first day already shows who rules creation.

feedbackWrong.default: The evaluation comes first; the names Day and Night close the movement.

options.a: God sees that the light is good
options.b: God separates the light from the darkness
options.c: God names the day and the night

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:7, which word confirms that God's command was fulfilled?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-05.learningObjective: Understand that God's command is fulfilled.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-05.feedbackCorrect: What God commands in 1:6 comes to pass in 1:7: his word is fulfilled.

feedbackWrong.a: It is not a beginning: it confirms that God's word was fulfilled.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of an end; it confirms the command came to pass.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-05.hint: Compare with what God commanded in the previous verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-06.question: What links Genesis 1:31 to 1 Timothy 4:4?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-06.learningObjective: Relate the goodness of creation in Genesis and in Paul.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul echoes Genesis: what God created is good and can be received with thanks.

feedbackWrong.a: Genesis calls everything God made very good, the material world included.
feedbackWrong.b: Both texts treat creation as real and good, not as mere appearance.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-06.hint: Compare what the two texts say about God's work.

options.a: Only the spiritual is good
options.b: Creation is mere appearance
options.c: The goodness of what God created

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-07.question: In Genesis 1:18, tap the role of the lights that repeats what God did in Genesis 1:4.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-07.learningObjective: Relate the fourth day to the first.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-07.feedbackCorrect: In 1:4 God separated light from darkness; on the fourth day the lights do that separating.

feedbackWrong.a: "Governar" is a new role given to the lights; it does not appear in 1:4.
feedbackWrong.b: "Isso era bom" is God's evaluation, not a role of the lights.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-07.hint: Reread Genesis 1:4 and look for the same idea here.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-08.question: How do the steps of Genesis 1:16–17 fit together?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-08.learningObjective: Understand how the text presents the heavenly bodies: made and serving.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-08.feedbackCorrect: God makes the heavenly bodies and sets them in the sky with a task: to light the earth.

feedbackWrong.default: First the two great lights, then the stars; their place and task come in 1:17.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-01-08.hint: Verse 17 says where God places them.

options.a: God makes the two great lights
options.b: God also makes the stars
options.c: God sets them in the sky to light the earth

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-01.question: In Genesis 1:9–10, the waters obey God's word and receive from him a place and a name.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-01.learningObjective: Interpret God's rule over the waters.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-01.feedbackCorrect: The waters go where God sends them and take the name he gives: nothing resists him.

feedbackWrong.false: The waters gather where God commands and he calls them Seas: they obey.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-01.hint: See what happens to the waters and who names them.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:29, tap the phrase that shows food is a gift from God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that provision is God's gift.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-02.feedbackCorrect: Food is not a human achievement: God says he himself gives it.

feedbackWrong.a: "Semente" describes the plants; the gift is in God's verb.
feedbackWrong.b: "Alimento" says what the plants are for; the gift is in what God does.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-02.hint: Look for the verb God uses when speaking of himself.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-03.question: What reading does Genesis 1:22 support about the fruitfulness of life?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about life that multiplies.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-03.feedbackCorrect: God blesses fish and birds so they will multiply: fruitfulness is his gift.

feedbackWrong.a: The text ties multiplying to blessing: "E Deus os abençoou, dizendo".
feedbackWrong.c: There is only one God in the text, and he is the one who blesses and commands to multiply.
feedbackWrong.d: In 1:22, the creatures of the waters and the birds are already blessed, before humans.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-03.hint: See where the command to multiply comes from.

options.a: Nature multiplies by its own power
options.b: Life multiplies as a blessing given by God
options.c: Fruitfulness comes from gods of nature
options.d: Only humans receive God's blessing

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-04.question: Which sequence reveals the path of the good creation in the Bible's story?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-04.learningObjective: See creation's goodness as the start of a thread that reaches the new creation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-04.feedbackCorrect: The good creation is wounded by sin, but God promises to renew all things.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1), fall (Gen 3:17) and new creation (Rev 21:5).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-04.hint: Follow the story: creation, fall, new creation.

options.a: God sees that his work is good
options.b: Because of sin, the ground is cursed
options.c: God promises to make all things new

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:16, what word does the text use for the heavenly bodies, without naming them?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows the heavenly bodies as creatures, not gods.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-05.feedbackCorrect: Neither sun nor moon is named: they are lights, objects that shine, made by God.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not treat the heavenly bodies as gods: God made them, as he made the stars.
feedbackWrong.c: They rule day and night, but as God's work, not as kings.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-05.hint: The heavenly bodies are described by what they do, not by what they are.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-06.question: What links Genesis 1:16 to Isaiah 40:26?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-06.learningObjective: Link the creation of the stars to the sovereign God who rules them.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah looks at the same stars as Genesis and sees the Creator who calls them by name.

feedbackWrong.b: Isaiah says not one of them is missing, because of God's great power.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts the stars are creatures; God is the one who rules.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-06.hint: See who, according to Isaiah, calls the stars by name.

options.a: The Creator rules even the stars
options.b: The stars escape God
options.c: The stars guide human fate

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-07.question: In Genesis 1:31, tap the word that shows how far God's approval reaches.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-07.learningObjective: Support from the text that all of creation is good.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-07.feedbackCorrect: God saw "tudo": nothing in creation is left out of the "muito bom".

feedbackWrong.b: "Muito bom" gives the degree of approval, not how far it reaches.
feedbackWrong.c: "Sexto dia" marks time, not the reach of the approval.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-08.question: Which sequence reveals the care of God that begins in Genesis 1:29?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-08.learningObjective: See God's care as a thread running through the Bible.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-08.feedbackCorrect: The God who gives food at creation keeps sustaining all he has made.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: creation (Gen 1:29), praise (Ps 145:15) and Jesus' teaching (Matt 6:26).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-01-08.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis, Psalms, Gospels.

options.a: God gives plants and fruit as food
options.b: The eyes of all look to God for food
options.c: The heavenly Father feeds the birds and cares for you

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-01.question: In Genesis 3:8, Adam and his wife hid from the Lord God among the trees of the garden.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-01.learningObjective: Observe the couple's reaction to God after disobeying.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-01.feedbackCorrect: After eating, the two hear God's voice and hide among the trees.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of 3:8: the two hid from the presence of the Lord God.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-01.hint: See what the couple does on hearing God's voice.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-02.question: In Genesis 2:15, tap the place where the Lord God put the man.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-02.learningObjective: Identify the garden as the place God prepared for the man.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-02.feedbackCorrect: God puts the man in the Garden of Eden with a task: to work it and keep it.

feedbackWrong.a: The Lord God is the one who puts him there; the question is where.
feedbackWrong.c: "O homem" is the one placed, not the place.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-02.hint: Look for a place with a proper name.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-03.question: According to Genesis 2:16–17, what did God say would happen on the day they ate from the forbidden tree?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-03.learningObjective: Observe the warning God gave about the tree.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-03.feedbackCorrect: God's warning is clear: on the day you eat of it, you will surely die.

feedbackWrong.a: The sweat appears in the sentence (3:19), not in the command of 2:17.
feedbackWrong.b: The serpent promises opened eyes (3:5), not God.
feedbackWrong.d: Leaving the garden comes later (3:23); God's warning speaks of death.

options.a: They would have to eat bread by sweat
options.b: Their eyes would be opened
options.c: They would surely die
options.d: They would be driven out of the garden

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-04.question: Put Genesis 3:24 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-04.feedbackCorrect: First the driving out; then the cherubim and the sword guarding the way.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the man's leaving; the sword comes at the end.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-04.hint: The verse begins with what happens to the man.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-05.question: In Genesis 3:7, what tree were the leaves the couple sewed together from?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-05.learningObjective: Remember how the couple tried to cover themselves after eating.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-05.feedbackCorrect: Fig leaves: the couple tries to cover their shame with what is at hand.

feedbackWrong.b: The olive leaf appears in the flood (Gen 8:11); here the leaves are from another tree.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not mention a vine; the leaves were from another tree.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-05.hint: Look at what they sewed to make coverings.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-06.question: What does Genesis 2:25 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-06.learningObjective: Link the innocence of 2:25 to the shame that arises in 3:7.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Before the fall they were naked and unashamed; what changes is the relationship, not the body.

feedbackWrong.a: Hiding from God only happens after eating (3:8).
feedbackWrong.b: 2:25 says the opposite: they were naked and felt no shame.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-06.hint: Compare what they felt before and after eating.

options.a: They were already hiding from God
options.b: Nakedness was always shameful
options.c: Before, there was innocence without shame

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-07.question: In Genesis 3:20, tap the name Adam gave his wife.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-07.learningObjective: Identify the name Adam gives the woman after the fall.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-07.feedbackCorrect: Adam calls her Eve, because she would be the mother of all human beings.

feedbackWrong.b: Adam is the one who gives the name; the name given is another.
feedbackWrong.c: "Seres humanos" explains the name: she is the mother of all.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-07.hint: Look for the name right after "o nome de".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-08.question: Put Genesis 2:22 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-08.feedbackCorrect: God takes the rib, forms the woman and brings her to Adam: he is the one who unites them.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the rib; the meeting with Adam comes at the end.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-02-08.hint: The verse begins with what God took from the man.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-01.question: In Genesis 3:10, Adam explains that he hid because he had eaten from the forbidden tree.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-01.learningObjective: Understand the link between fear, shame and hiding in 3:10.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-01.feedbackCorrect: Adam gives another reason: he was naked and afraid; he does not confess that he ate.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 3:10: "porque estava nu, tive medo". He only admits it in 3:12, blaming the woman.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-01.hint: See the reason that comes after "porque".

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-02.question: In Genesis 3:23, tap the phrase that links leaving the garden to what God has just said.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-02.learningObjective: Recognize the link between God's decision and leaving the garden.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-02.feedbackCorrect: "Por isso" links leaving Eden to the decision in 3:22 about the tree of life.

feedbackWrong.a: "A fim de" says what the man leaves for, to work the ground; it does not link back.
feedbackWrong.c: "Enviou" is the action; the link to 3:22 is the phrase between commas.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-02.hint: Look for a short phrase between commas.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-03.question: In Genesis 3:12–13, what do the answers of Adam and the woman have in common?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-03.learningObjective: Understand how sin leads each one to shift the blame.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Adam points to the woman; the woman points to the serpent. No one takes the blame.

feedbackWrong.a: Neither asks for forgiveness; each points to someone else.
feedbackWrong.b: Both admit "e eu comi", but only after blaming someone else.
feedbackWrong.d: Only the woman accuses the serpent; Adam points to the woman.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-03.hint: See whom each one points to before saying "e eu comi".

options.a: Both confess and ask forgiveness
options.b: Both deny they ate
options.c: Each one passes the blame to another
options.d: Both accuse the serpent

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-04.question: How do the movements of Genesis 3:22–23 fit together?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement that leads to leaving Eden.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-04.feedbackCorrect: God assesses, guards the tree of life and sends the man to work the ground he came from.

feedbackWrong.default: The assessment comes first (3:22); leaving the garden closes the passage (3:23).

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-04.hint: The passage begins with God speaking.

options.a: God notes that the man knows good and evil
options.b: God blocks access to the tree of life
options.c: The man leaves the garden to work the ground

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-05.question: In Genesis 3:11, which verb shows the problem was disobeying God?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-05.learningObjective: Understand that the fall is disobedience to a command of God.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-05.feedbackCorrect: God recalls the command he gave: the heart of sin is disobedience.

feedbackWrong.b: More than a warning: God gave a command, and the couple disobeyed it.
feedbackWrong.c: It was not a request: it was a command from God (2:16–17).

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-05.hint: Recall how Genesis 2:16 describes God speaking to the man.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-06.question: What links Genesis 3:8 to Proverbs 28:13?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-06.learningObjective: Relate the hiding in Eden to the biblical call to confession.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Hiding solves nothing; Proverbs points the other way: confess and find mercy.

feedbackWrong.a: Proverbs says the opposite: whoever confesses and forsakes sin finds mercy.
feedbackWrong.c: God goes after the one who hides (3:9); Proverbs says concealing does not prosper.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-06.hint: Compare what the couple does with what Proverbs says of the one who conceals.

options.a: Confessing only brings more punishment
options.b: Hiding sin solves nothing
options.c: God approves of those who hide

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-07.question: In Genesis 2:17, tap the word that marks the exception to the freedom given in 2:16.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-07.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast between wide freedom and the single prohibition.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-07.feedbackCorrect: "Mas" opens the exception: they could eat from every tree but one.

feedbackWrong.a: "Certamente" reinforces the warning; it does not mark the exception.
feedbackWrong.b: "Porque" gives the reason for the prohibition; the exception starts earlier.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-07.hint: See how the verse connects to the one before.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-08.question: How do the couple's reactions in Genesis 3:7–8 fit together?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-08.learningObjective: Understand how shame leads from covering up to fleeing God.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-08.feedbackCorrect: Shame comes first, then the attempt to cover up, and finally fleeing from God.

feedbackWrong.default: First they notice they are naked (3:7); the hiding comes when they hear God (3:8).

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-02-08.hint: Start with what happens to their eyes.

options.a: The two realize they are naked
options.b: They try to cover themselves with leaves
options.c: On hearing God, they hide

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-01.question: In Genesis 3:12, by speaking of "mulher que me deste", Adam lays part of the blame on God himself.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-01.learningObjective: Interpret Adam's answer as blame-shifting that reaches God.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-01.feedbackCorrect: "A mulher que me deste": Adam points to the woman and, behind her, to the one who gave her.

feedbackWrong.false: Notice "que me deste": Adam reminds God that he was the one who gave him the woman.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-01.hint: Notice how Adam describes the woman.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-02.question: In Genesis 3:22, tap the phrase that says what God wants to prevent by guarding the tree of life.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that leaving Eden also prevents living forever in the fall.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-02.feedbackCorrect: God keeps the man from living forever in his fallen state: leaving also protects.

feedbackWrong.a: "Um de Nós" describes the situation; what God wants to prevent comes at the end.
feedbackWrong.b: Knowing good and evil has already happened; what God wants to prevent comes after.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-02.hint: Look for what would follow eating from the tree of life.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-03.question: What reading does Genesis 3:23–24 support about leaving Eden?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading that sees judgment and hope in leaving Eden.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Leaving is judgment, but the tree is guarded, not destroyed: the way to life still exists.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says God sent him out and drove him out; it was not the man's choice.
feedbackWrong.c: God clothes the couple before they leave (3:21) and gives the man work: no abandonment.
feedbackWrong.d: The cherubim guard the way to the tree; it is still there.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-03.hint: See what the cherubim and the sword do.

options.a: The man leaves the garden by his own decision
options.b: There is judgment, but the tree of life is guarded
options.c: God abandons the man forever, with no care at all
options.d: The tree of life is destroyed after the fall
