genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-04.question: Which sequence reveals who covers human shame?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-04.learningObjective: See the act of 3:21 as the start of a thread: God covers those who cannot cover themselves.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-04.feedbackCorrect: Leaves are not enough; God himself clothes the couple, and later clothes his people with salvation.

feedbackWrong.default: From human effort (Gen 3:7) to God's care (Gen 3:21) and to salvation (Isa 61:10).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-04.hint: Start with what the couple does on their own.

options.a: The couple covers themselves with leaves they sew
options.b: God himself covers the man and woman with skins
options.c: God clothes his people with garments of salvation

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-05.question: In Genesis 3:21, what did the Lord God make for Adam and his wife?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-05.learningObjective: Remember God's act of care in the midst of judgment.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-05.feedbackCorrect: After the judgment, God himself clothes the couple: grace appears before they leave the garden.

feedbackWrong.b: Coverings were what the couple made of leaves (3:7); God makes something better, of skins.
feedbackWrong.c: God gives not shelter but clothes: he himself dresses them.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-05.hint: See what God does at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-06.question: What links Genesis 3:9 to Luke 19:10?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-06.learningObjective: Link God's call in Eden to Jesus' mission to seek the lost.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-06.feedbackCorrect: God calls the one who hid in Eden; in Jesus, he comes to seek and save the lost.

feedbackWrong.a: The ones hiding in Eden had sinned; Jesus came precisely for the lost.
feedbackWrong.b: In both texts the initiative is God's: he calls and comes seeking.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-06.hint: Compare who takes the initiative in both texts.

options.a: Only the righteous are sought
options.b: God waits for man to come back alone
options.c: God seeks those who are lost

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-07.question: In Genesis 3:10, tap the phrase that shows God's presence came to frighten the man.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-07.learningObjective: Support from the text that sin turns God's presence into a threat.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-07.feedbackCorrect: Before there was fellowship; now God's voice brings fear. Sin changed the relationship.

feedbackWrong.a: God's voice is not the problem; the problem is what it now stirs in the man.
feedbackWrong.c: "No jardim" says where; the man's reaction comes after.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-07.hint: Look for the feeling the man confesses.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-08.question: Which sequence reveals the path from death to life starting from Genesis 2:17?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-08.learningObjective: See the death announced in Eden in light of the resurrection in Christ.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-08.feedbackCorrect: The warning comes true in the return to dust, but in Christ there is resurrection.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: warning (Gen 2:17), sentence (Gen 3:19) and resurrection (1 Cor 15:22).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-02-08.hint: Start with God's warning in the garden.

options.a: God warns that eating from the tree brings death
options.b: The man hears he will return to dust
options.c: In Christ, all will be raised

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-01.question: In Genesis 3:6, the woman ate the fruit alone, without her husband there with her.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-01.learningObjective: Observe that the man and the woman take part in the disobedience together.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says she gave "também ao marido que estava com ela, e ele comeu".

feedbackWrong.true: Reread the end of 3:6: her husband was with her and ate too.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-02.question: In Genesis 4:8, tap who killed his own brother.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-02.learningObjective: Identify the first murderer in the Bible.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-02.feedbackCorrect: Cain rises against Abel: the sin of the fall already reaches violence between brothers.

feedbackWrong.b: Abel is the brother who was killed, not the one who killed.
feedbackWrong.c: The field is where it happened, not who acted.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-02.hint: Look for who rose up against the other.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-03.question: According to Genesis 1:31, how did God assess everything he had made?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-03.feedbackCorrect: God looks at the whole work and says it was very good: the world begins good, not broken.

feedbackWrong.a: Nothing needed fixing before the disobedience of Genesis 3.
feedbackWrong.b: The text sees no danger in creation; the verdict is "muito bom".
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of unfinished work; the verdict is "muito bom".

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-03.hint: Read the verdict in the middle of the verse.

options.a: In need of repair
options.b: Beautiful, but dangerous
options.c: Good, but still incomplete
options.d: Very good

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-04.question: Put Genesis 2:7 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-04.feedbackCorrect: God forms from dust, breathes the breath of life, and the man comes alive.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the dust of the ground; the living man closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-04.hint: The verse moves from dust to life.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-05.question: In Genesis 11:4, what did the people want to build along with the city?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-05.feedbackCorrect: A tower with its top in the heavens: the symbol of a people who wanted to rise without God.

feedbackWrong.a: It was not a house; it was a structure whose top would reach the heavens.
feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of a wall; it speaks of something tall, its top in the heavens.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-05.hint: See what had a top that would reach the heavens.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-06.question: What does Genesis 12:1 communicate that links to this context?
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-06.learningObjective: Link Genesis 12:1 to the new beginning after Babel.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-06.feedbackCorrect: After the scattered peoples, the story starts again with a word from God: "Saia".

feedbackWrong.b: God asks the opposite: to leave his relatives and his father's house.
feedbackWrong.c: Building a city was Babel's plan; Abram is called to set out.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-06.hint: See what the Lord asks of Abram.

options.a: God calls Abram to leave
options.b: Abram stays with his family
options.c: Abram builds a city

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-07.question: In Genesis 6:9, tap whom Noah walked with.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-07.feedbackCorrect: In the middle of a violent generation, Noah walked with God.

feedbackWrong.a: "Gerações" opens the story of Noah's family; it does not say whom he walked with.
feedbackWrong.b: Noah lived among his contemporaries, but the text says whom he walked with.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-07.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-08.question: Put Genesis 12:2 in the order of the text.
genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-08.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: the nation, the blessing with a great name, and Abram as a blessing.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the great nation; "você será uma bênção" closes the verse.

genesis-1-11-sem-gen-boss-final-08.hint: The verse begins with what God will make of Abram.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-01.question: In Genesis 3:23, leaving the garden appears as a consequence of what happened before.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-01.learningObjective: Understand leaving Eden as a consequence of disobedience.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-01.feedbackCorrect: "Por isso" links leaving the garden to the disobedience told before.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of 3:23: "por isso" links the leaving to what happened before.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-01.hint: Look for the phrase between commas at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-02.question: In Genesis 4:7, tap the word that opens the other side of the choice before Cain.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-02.learningObjective: Recognize the contrast marker in the warning to Cain.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-02.feedbackCorrect: "Mas" turns the sentence: on one side, doing well; on the other, sin at the door.

feedbackWrong.a: "Porta" shows where sin crouches, not the turn of the sentence.
feedbackWrong.c: "Se" opens the first side of the choice, that of doing well.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-02.hint: Look for the word right after the first question.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-03.question: How does Genesis 3:15 relate to the disobedience in Genesis 3:6?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-03.learningObjective: Relate the fall to the promise given within the judgment.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-03.feedbackCorrect: The judgment on the serpent already brings hope: the woman's offspring will crush its head.

feedbackWrong.a: The serpent strikes the heel, but its head is crushed: it does not win.
feedbackWrong.b: Sin has real consequences; the promise comes within the judgment.
feedbackWrong.c: The text speaks of conflict and wounds, not of a life without suffering.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-03.hint: Compare what happens to the head and to the heel.

options.a: God declares the serpent has won for good
options.b: God undoes sin as if nothing had happened
options.c: God promises the woman will never suffer again
options.d: Amid the judgment, God announces the serpent's defeat

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-04.question: How does the story of Genesis move on from Genesis 1:31?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from good creation to the spread of sin.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-04.feedbackCorrect: From the very good creation comes disobedience, and from it, an earth full of violence (6:11).

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the good creation; the violence filling the earth comes after the fall.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-04.hint: Sin grows: first one act, then the whole earth.

options.a: God creates everything very good
options.b: Disobedience enters the world
options.c: Violence fills the earth

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-05.question: In Genesis 3:6, what action comes right after the woman looks at the tree?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-05.learningObjective: Understand the step from desire to action in the fall.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-05.feedbackCorrect: The look becomes desire, and desire becomes action: she reaches out and takes the fruit.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of harvesting; it shows the hand taking what was forbidden.
feedbackWrong.b: Eating comes next; before that, the text shows the hand taking the fruit.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-05.hint: See what the woman does right after desiring the fruit.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-06.question: What links Genesis 3:6 to Romans 5:12?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-06.learningObjective: Relate the fall in Genesis 3 to Paul's reading of it.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-06.feedbackCorrect: Paul rereads Genesis 3: through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin.

feedbackWrong.a: Paul speaks of "one man"; the man also ate (Gen 3:6).
feedbackWrong.c: Paul says the opposite: through sin, death spread to all.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-06.hint: See what Paul says entered the world.

options.a: Only the woman sinned
options.b: Sin enters the world
options.c: Sin fades over time

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-07.question: In Genesis 11:8, tap the word that links the scattering to God's decision in 11:7.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-07.learningObjective: Recognize the result marker at Babel.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-07.feedbackCorrect: "Assim" shows the result: what God decided in 11:7 happens in 11:8.

feedbackWrong.a: "Cessaram" shows the effect on the work, not the link to the decision.
feedbackWrong.c: "Dali" shows where the peoples left from, not the link to 11:7.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-07.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-08.question: How does the story move from Babel to Abram's call?
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-08.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between Babel and Abram's call.
genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-08.feedbackCorrect: The name Babel tried to win becomes God's promise to Abram, after the scattering.

feedbackWrong.default: Babel comes first (11:4 and 11:8); the promise to Abram comes in 12:2.

genesis-1-11-cam-gen-boss-final-08.hint: The name appears twice: first as ambition, then as gift.

options.a: The people want to make a name for themselves
options.b: God scatters the peoples over the earth
options.c: God promises to make Abram's name great

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-01.question: In Genesis 3:8–9, after the disobedience, God withdraws and leaves humans alone.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-01.learningObjective: Interpret God's response to sin as seeking, not abandonment.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-01.feedbackCorrect: God comes to the garden and calls: "Onde você está?". The one who hides is the human.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread 3:9: the Lord God called the man. The one who withdraws is the human.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-01.hint: See who hides and who calls.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-02.question: In Genesis 3:15, tap the one the promise points to as the serpent's conqueror.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-02.learningObjective: Support from the text the hope announced in Genesis 3:15.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-02.feedbackCorrect: The woman's offspring crushes the serpent's head: victory comes from her line.

feedbackWrong.a: "Tua descendência" is the serpent's, which only strikes the heel.
feedbackWrong.b: "Inimizade" describes the conflict, not who wins.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-02.hint: See who strikes the head, not the heel.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-03.question: In light of Genesis 1–11, what reading does Genesis 12:2–3 support?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading that links Genesis 1–11 to the promise to Abram.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-03.feedbackCorrect: After the fall, the flood and Babel, God promises to bless all families of the earth.

feedbackWrong.a: At each fall God acts: he clothes, protects, preserves and, here, promises blessing.
feedbackWrong.b: The promise reaches all families of the earth through Abram.
feedbackWrong.d: God speaks, calls and promises: he is not a God who abandoned the world.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-03.hint: Compare each option with the end of 12:3.

options.a: Genesis 1–11 is just a collection of failures
options.b: God leaves the other peoples to keep Abram
options.c: God does not give up and opens a way of blessing
options.d: After sin, God abandoned the world

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-04.question: Which sequence reveals the thread of the promise that begins in Genesis 3:15?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-04.learningObjective: See the promise as a thread running from the fall to the new creation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-04.feedbackCorrect: The promise is born in judgment (3:15), takes a face in Abram (12:3) and ends in all things new.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the Bible: the fall (Gen 3:15), Abram (Gen 12:3) and the new creation (Rev 21:5).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Genesis 3, Genesis 12, Revelation.

options.a: God announces the serpent's defeat
options.b: God promises blessing to all families in Abram
options.c: God makes all things new

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-05.question: In Genesis 12:3, what will happen to all the families of the earth?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the promise for the peoples.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-05.feedbackCorrect: The families scattered at Babel will be blessed: the promise answers Genesis 1–11.

feedbackWrong.b: Judgment marked Genesis 1–11; here God promises the opposite for the families.
feedbackWrong.c: God does not forget the scattered peoples; he promises to reach them.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-05.hint: See what God promises at the end of the verse.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-06.question: What links Genesis 3:17 to Revelation 22:3?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-06.learningObjective: Link the curse of the fall to its end in the new creation.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-06.feedbackCorrect: The curse that begins in Genesis 3 ends at the close of the Bible: no curse ever again.

feedbackWrong.a: Genesis 3:17 states the curse; Revelation announces its end.
feedbackWrong.b: Revelation says the opposite: "there will no longer be any curse".

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-06.hint: Compare the start and the end of the Bible on the curse.

options.a: The ground was never cursed
options.b: The curse lasts forever
options.c: The end of the curse

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-07.question: In Genesis 4:7, tap the phrase that shows Cain could still resist sin.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-07.learningObjective: Support from the text human responsibility in the face of sin.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-07.feedbackCorrect: "Você deve dominá-lo": sin prowls, but Cain is still responsible and can resist.

feedbackWrong.a: "À porta" shows sin close by, not the chance to resist.
feedbackWrong.c: "Deseja você" shows the force of sin, not Cain's response.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-07.hint: See what God says Cain must do.

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-08.question: Which sequence reveals how God responds to sin before Abram?
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-08.learningObjective: See the pattern of judgment and care in Genesis 1–11.
genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-08.feedbackCorrect: At each stage, God judges sin and yet keeps the story open.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow Genesis: the garden (Gen 3), the flood (Gen 6) and Babel (Gen 11).

genesis-1-11-pro-gen-boss-final-08.hint: Follow the order of the chapters of Genesis.

options.a: Humans disobey and lose the garden
options.b: God judges violence, but preserves Noah
options.c: God checks Babel's pride and scatters the peoples
